items.title: Partial dungeon rewards: my reading of note 21
items.body: Your note: "%completed * 0.5 ... If only 1-3rd map completed, 0.25". Built: f = parts won / parts. All parts: full rewards. 1-3 parts won: f x 0.25. More, short of all (4 of 5): f x 0.5. So 4/5 pays 40%, 3/5 15%, 2/5 10%, 1/5 5%. The other reading of "1-3rd" is "a third or less" (f <= 1/3: x 0.25, else x 0.5: 3/5 would pay 30%). One table in bramblewood-coop.js (RUN_PAY_BANDS).
options: A third or less: x 0.25, otherwise x 0.5

items.title: Inspiring as Inspiration tokens: the reading built
items.body: Owner 20:28: "Inspiring - +2 attack to adjacent creatures. It stacks! Once unit attacks and hits something, the inspiring tokens are expended for N damage. There should be a inspiration vfx effect on the card numbers." Built (ENG21) in the simplest reading: tokens are still given when the Inspiring unit attacks (the old text said so; not On Ready); Inspiring N gives each adjacent ally (left / right, plus front / behind where the rows fight) N Inspiration tokens, +2 Attack each, and they stack with no cap; the ally spends them all when its attack lands a hit on a unit or the bramble (the extra Attack counts on every hit of that swing); a miss, a dodge or a swing with no target keeps them. Before: +N Attack, spent by the next swing even if it missed. A 📯N pip shows them; the Attack number glows as they come and flares as they go. Price (400 paired fights, bramble 15): Inspiring 1 3.3 -> 5.43, Inspiring 2 5.96 -> 6.99 (pow 0.364). No card was re-fitted: Otter Flag-Bearer (96% -> 107% of its budget) and Meerkat Wayfarer (99% -> 113%) are now over; Conch Herald was over already (111% -> 121%), and so was ENG22's Cricket Drummer (2/7, 124% -> 140%, held by ENG22-4). The Whetstone kit item shares the bonus field: its +1 now also lasts until a landing hit.
options: Tokens on Ready, not on attack
+N Attack a token (N = Attack, one token)
Spent by any swing, a miss too
items.answer: As built: tokens are given when the Inspiring unit attacks. Owner 2026-11-04 22:34: "Tokens given on unit with inspiration N attacks."

items.title: On Attack goes off after the swing
items.body: Owner 22:15 #12: "On attack triggers happen after attack. For example draw. You should immediately draw a card." Built: a unit's On Attack triggers go off right after its swing (and the swing's answers: Thorns, a counter, Sweep / Fork prongs), both sides. Before, they went off as it committed to the swing, before the blow; and the page only redrew your hand after the round, so a drawn card looked like next turn's draw. Now it lands in your hand as the draw plays in the replay. Fire on hit still goes off before the blow (it loads that swing). A swing that finds nothing still fires them. Silence / Stymie / Exhaust / Petrify (On Attack, adjacent enemies) now land after the hit, so the struck unit's Thorns and on-hit answers still go off that swing. A unit that dies in its own swing still draws, gains or hits, but gives itself nothing (heal, buff, Shield, cleanse).

A unit killed in its swing fires nothing
items.outcome: Claude's call (owner 11-03 09:39: 'Balance items you can choose. Like ENG and FIX and UI.'): Keep (as built): On Attack goes off after the swing.

items.title: Fire and water: the numbers (built as proposed)
items.body: Owner 22:44: "Fire damage should light the target on fire, or remove wet counters first. (Tide and Ebb add a water counter if the card doesn't have counters - flood up to max 2 counters, ebb up to max 1) (Water damage adds water counters = damage)". Built (ENG20): a unit holds up to 3 water counters (💧N pip); water damage adds counters equal to the damage and puts Burn out. At a round's start a unit in the water with no counter gets 2 in a Flood or High Tide, 1 in an Ebb (only Swimmer / Tide units are in the water in an Ebb); a unit that has counters gets none, and counters stay until fire dries them (they no longer vanish when the tide goes out). Wet = its counters (a Swimmer / Tide unit is always at least 1) + 1 under Rain; each lightning hit still gets +1 a Wet counter. A fire hit that lands dries 1 counter a point; if points are left once the unit is dry and the fire came from a unit (a swing, shot or skill), it is Burning (🔥 pip): 1 fire at the start of each of the next 2 rounds; a new fire hit refreshes it to 2, it never stacks. Field fire (Scorching, the volcano, Wildfire) dries but lights nothing; a unit that resists fire (Resist, Immune, Dry) never burns; Cleanse removes Burn. Cards affected: the 19 fire attackers and 17 fire-skill cards hit harder (about +2 a lit target), the 29 fire-resistant cards are spared; on tidal maps land units now stay Wet (2) after a Flood, so the 9 lightning cards hit them harder; Tide Spirit and the 5 Wave / Tsunami cards now soak their targets (shielding them from Burn).
options: Fire dries one counter a hit (not a point)
Counters dry by 1 at each Ebb
items.outcome: Claude's call (owner 11-03 09:39: 'Balance items you can choose. Like ENG and FIX and UI.'): As built (fire dries a counter a point, Burn 2 rounds, cap 3).
items.answer: Owner 2026-11-03 22:02: "Wetness is lost 1 per turn." Built (ENG22): each unit loses 1 water counter at every round start, before the tide adds counters, on top of fire drying them.

Glean 🫐 (owner 22:47: "takes any berry counter it can on the map to +1 shield"): every turn while Ready it takes every Berry on the board, both sides, any row (Berries have no range rule; only Foraging makes them, Pickpocket steals them on a hit) and gains +1 Shield each; 0.3 fixed. items.body: Owner 22:44: "if a defensive (+0/N) buff is removed and the unit would die, they remain with 1 health instead. Damage dealt to it always prioritises the buff-health, not the true health. Otherwise, debuffs can sometimes kill units." Built as a cap: when a live +0/N buff shrinks or ends the unit keeps its Health up to the new maximum, never below 1, so a hit that landed during the buff came off the buff first. Now on Nature's Force, Kinship, Pack / Pack Leader, Formation, Herald and the Crosswind; the Zeitgeber / state Health and an equipped piece already worked this way. Before, those five auras took their whole N off the unit's Health (never below 1). Debuffs, Wither and Isolation deepening still take Health. Built (ENG18): every Baby card (kind baby, 21 incl. the eggs and the starter babies Otter Kit and Duckling) has base Level 0 (cardBaseLevel): its printed stats are its Level 0 stats and Hatchling is a Level 0 skill (levelSkills "0"; older overrides at Level 1 read as Level 0, eng17MigrateHatchling). Done in BAL11. | After BAL10's retune 87 of 226 fights (Maps 0-20) are still more than 20 points off, nearly all too hard: The Canopy 3% (target 68), The Sunken Depths 18%, The Mycelium Deep 26%, The Pale Desert 30%, Wolfsbane Tundra 31%, Basalt Foundry 36%, Caves & Alcoves 38%, and many first fights (4-1, 8-1, 10-1 at 37-55% against 90). Under the fight's own list, K14 (non-unique cards 1 copy, 6 in all) and 5-7 distinct cards, the curve search had no legal move left on 129 of 155 off fights. A side map's list cards mostly count as non-unique for K14, so its decks cannot swap down.
options: a) Allow a lower enemy bramble Health (at most 40% off) on too-hard fights only.
b) Let a side map's own list count as map-unique for K14.
c) Rebuild the Map reference decks (the yardstick may be too weak after BAL9's cut swaps; Reference Random agrees on Maps 4, 14, 17).

items.title: Baby cards and the egg's Hatch or Stay: the details
items.body: Owner 11-02 (JJ25, replaces BABY-1): "Baby cards can be levelled 0 -> 1 -> 10. Getting an egg (and at each level-up) offers Hatch or Stay (the egg shakes); staying lets it level as an egg, for Evomax decks."
options: a) Every new copy of a Baby card comes at Level 0 (the Nest trains 0 -> 1, the Forge 1 -> 10; the starter babies too, no Base cap of 4). An egg card (egg-*) asks when a copy arrives and at each level-up of that copy (Forge or Nest); the question waits until no fight or dialog is up. Hatch: that copy becomes its creature (the fixed hatch, or a random Common / Uncommon map or pack card of its kind, as the engine's egg rule) at the egg's level; Stay: it stays an egg.
items.outcome: a) Coordinator call (ENG16). Open: what an egg is worth at Lv 10 in battle (it still cracks into a random creature when Ready, at its own stats); Evomax decks may want a hatch that keeps a level bonus. Hatching removes the egg copy, so a deck that held it shows one copy short until rebuilt.

items.title: Milling and the wind: the details
items.body: Owner 11-02 (JJ17): "Milling: turns 1 of your Lumber into 2 Lumber; its skill worth x0.85"; WIND-2 (a).
options: a) Milling N: each turn while Ready, N of the Lumber you hold become 2N (net +N); with no Lumber nothing happens; Lumberjack still adds. Price: mult 1.54 -> 1.31 (x0.85), not re-measured. Wind: the Headwind's -1 Attack is on its swing (effAtk), not on fixed shots (Arrow N stays N); Quiet Contemplation no longer touches the wind (nothing doubles).
items.outcome: a) Coordinator call (ENG16). Re-measure Milling and the wind with the next skill measure.

b) As the owner wrote: headwind = Quick, tailwind = -1 Attack.

items.body: Owner 11-02 14:10: "Hatchling doesn't do that. It just does what we wanted Fodder to do." Hatchling replaces Fodder: the Baby card is feed for an Evomax evolute (Stem from Level 1), no growing into an adult card. Coordinator draft: Hatchling (Grows into X): after N rounds on the board (or N wins in the collection), it grows into its adult card; an Evomax creature's first stage is a Hatchling. Owner to shape the rule; until then the card group label (Baby) is the only marker.

items.title: Seven in-play cards: their re-priced skills alone break cap 2
items.body: SKILL2 re-priced the skills in 3A + H stat points (BUDGET2-1 / BUDGET2-2). Cap 2 is A*H x m + S*|S| <= 1.57 x (N/3)^2: S is squared, so a skill price that rises x1.5-2 raises its cap-2 term x2-4. For seven in-play cards no stat line fits any more (or only one that takes over 40% of the card): Alley Cat 2/2 (Twin Strike 3.17 -> 6.99), Tide-pool Crab 1/3, Owl Nightwatch 1/5, Bee Forager 0/5 (On Attack -> Heal x8.2), Conch Crawler 2/2, Gatling Hog 2/9 (Twin Strike), Ant Warrior 2/4 (only 1/1 fits). They are left as they are and listed in docs/balance/skill2-refit-2026-10-31.json `held` (with the Caldera Wyrm, your over-on-purpose card). BUDGET2 kept cap 2 where it was when the stats changed scale (cap2Mult 2 -> 1.57); the same here would read S in the old currency: (S/2)*|S/2|.
options: Cap 2 reads S / 2 (keeps cap 2 where it was before the currency change; bramblewood-budget.js, one constant)
Trim a skill on each of the seven (a card-data package)
items.default: Cap 2 reads S / 2 (keeps cap 2 where it was before the currency change; bramblewood-budget.js, one constant)
items.outcome: Coordinator (owner's standing 'fill in the decisions'): cap 2 reads S / 2, the same scale fix BUDGET2 made for stats. One constant in bramblewood-budget.js; the seven cards then re-fit in BAL8.

items.title: Flying and Evasive measure at a third of their price
items.body: Flying (83 in-play cards) and Evasive (22) are priced as a multiplier on the stats (MISS_MULT_BY in bramblewood-budget.js: Flying x1.39, your estimate; Evasive x1.37), 10.4 points on the canon's carriers. The SKILL2 measure (1,000 paired fights, the placebo taken out) reads Flying 3.56 [3.32, 3.81] and Evasive 3.42 [3.11, 3.66]: about x1.13. This is why Gannet Cliffs' flyers sat under the fair line (DECK1-5): the DECK1-5 lifts (Peak Condor 4/7, Hawk Arrowkeeper 2/8, Red-billed Chough 3/2, Peregrine Stooper 2/8) put them at 112-123% of N on paper. SKILL2 measured these for the record only (a budget constant); nothing changed.
options: Set Flying and Evasive to the measured x1.13 (every flyer gains room; a card pass then lifts the flyers that fall well under)
items.default: Set Flying and Evasive to the measured x1.13 (every flyer gains room; a card pass then lifts the flyers that fall well under)
items.outcome: Coordinator: set Flying and Evasive to the measured x1.13; a flyer card pass follows (in BAL8). The DECK1-5 lifts then sit near 100% of N.

items.title: Armor measures concave, not 'slightly exponential'
items.body: ENG9-9 (your rule): Armor is 1.68 x N^1.43, 'slightly exponential as 5 armor nullifies most damage'. The shared canon measure (BUDGET2-2) reads Armor 1 / 2 / 3 at 2.65 / 4.23 / 4.84 stat points: each point is worth less than the one before. The canon (Armor 1 and 2) now fixes the curve at 2.65 x N^0.675 (Armor 3 5.56, 4 6.75, 5 7.84; your rule gave 8.1 / 12.2 / 16.8 in the old currency). Armor 4-5 were not measured (no in-play card).
options: Keep the canon at 1-2 and your x N^1.43 shape above 2
items.outcome: Coordinator: measure Armor 4-5 first (one canon-tool run, part of SPEED1's first pipeline run); keep the measured curve at 1-3 meanwhile.

items.title: Field and partner skills read low on vanilla carriers: measure them on their home maps?
items.body: The canon measure plays every road fight's field at its share, on vanilla carriers. Skills that need a field, a map or partners read low there: Tide 0.42 (price 1.5, 49 cards), Mountain Climber 0.37 (4), Dry 0.34 (4), Darksight 0.25 (3), Fog 0.08 (2.7), Kinship 0.86 (3), Guardian -0.82 (0), plus 18 more listed in docs/balance/skill2-prices-2026-10-31.json `kept`. SKILL2 raised such a skill when it read higher and kept its price otherwise. A home-map measure (the canon tool's --map N: the anchors played again in that map's context, about 15 minutes a map) would price them on the maps where they are played.
options: Measure them on their home maps (a follow-up package)
items.default: Measure them on their home maps (a follow-up package)
items.outcome: Coordinator: yes, home-map measures, run as a SPEED1 pipeline step (canon tool --map N) rather than an agent package.

items.title: Skill prices are in the old currency (Attack = 2)
items.body: BUDGET2 moved the stats to 3A + H and fitted N (x 1.13) with skill prices unchanged. The prices were measured in 2A + H points: RECOST1's yardstick valued a point at 4.17 win-rate points (+1 Attack 9.5, +1 Health 3.0); a 3A + H point is (9.5 + 3.0) / 4 = 3.1, so in the new currency a measured price would be about x1.33. The canon check (tools/skill_canon_2026_10_31.js, 200 paired fights on 6 vanilla carriers) reads more: a point of skill price buys about 2.2 points of stats (kappa 0.46 [0.38, 0.58]). Cheap skills next to stats make cards with skills stronger than vanilla cards of the same budget. docs/balance/budget2-2026-10-31.md sections 5 and 6.
options: Scale every measured price x1.33 and re-fit (a second full re-fit, N re-fitted)
Re-measure the skills against the re-canonised anchors (BUDGET2-2) and re-fit then
items.default: Re-measure the skills against the re-canonised anchors (BUDGET2-2) and re-fit then
items.outcome: Coordinator (owner's standing 'fill in the decisions'): re-measure every skill price against the anchors (after BUDGET2-2), in package SKILL2. No blanket x1.33.

items.title: Re-canonise the anchor skills from one shared measure?
items.body: X14: 12 canon anchors (15 points) are marked in canonical/skill-costs.json (canon: true): Armor 1/2, Poison 1/2, Bleed 1/2, Regen 2, Pounce 2, Quick, Sweep 2, Fork, Rage, Inspiring 1, Gold on Ready 1, Shell 2. On one shared set of carriers their RECOST1 prices disagree: 13 of 15 fall outside the interval the other anchors give them (Sweep 2 reads 2.9 vs price 1.1, Fork 3.0 vs 1.27, Gold on Ready 3.1 vs 2.31, Rage 2.0 vs 0.99; Armor 2 2.1 vs 4.53, Poison 1 1.2 vs 3.0). RECOST1 measured each on its own carriers. A canon is only a yardstick if its prices come from one measure.
options: Re-canonise: each anchor's canon price = its worth in this shared measure at 400 fights, scaled so the anchors' total stays
Keep the RECOST1 prices as canon; read the tool's results as relative only
Shrink the canon to the anchors that agree (Pounce 2, Quick) and add others
items.default: Re-canonise: each anchor's canon price = its worth in this shared measure at 400 fights, scaled so the anchors' total stays
items.outcome: Coordinator (owner's standing 'fill in the decisions'): yes, re-set the anchors' prices from one shared measurement first (SKILL2).

items.title: War Elephant: one arrow now; price Arrow Count as one more shot?
items.body: X15 / RECOST1-5 ("if you can cut the arrow count, do it"): War Elephant now fires one Arrow 2 a round (Arrow Count 2 -> 1), 0/28, 85% of N. Arrow Count is priced 'half', 6 a point: Arrow Count 2 costs 12 for one extra shot that Arrow 2 alone prices at 6. Priced as (N - 1) x the arrow's own price, Arrow Count 2 would cost 6 and the Elephant fits with both arrows (cap 1 44.5 <= 45.2, cap 2 273 <= 356). Only card with Arrow Count.
options: Price Arrow Count as (N - 1) x the arrow's price and give the second arrow back
items.default: Price Arrow Count as (N - 1) x the arrow's price and give the second arrow back
items.outcome: Coordinator (owner's standing 'fill in the decisions'): no. The owner asked to cut the arrow count (X15); War Elephant keeps 1 arrow.

items.title: Cottontail: 2/5 or 3/1?
items.body: Cottontail (T-1 / T-2 card, 4/2) must fit at Level 0 too (SKL0-1): 3A + H <= 10.68. The re-fit's rule (smallest relative change, then Health back for the Attack cut) gave 2/5 (89% of N at Level 1). 3/1 also fits (81%) and keeps the fast, fragile rabbit. Pond Trout (3/4 -> 2/5) has the same choice (3/1).
items.outcome: Coordinator (owner's standing 'fill in the decisions'): keep 2/5. Tutorial cards that survive a hit teach better than 3/1 glass.

items.body: RECOST1-6's second half: the Marshal (Epic, Armor 2, Sweep 4, 2/3) was under its band before BUDGET2 and stays there (45% of N 33.71 at 3A + H). BUDGET2 re-fit only what its formula pushed out. A lift to about 80% of N is 4/9 or 3/12.

items.title: A small arena_app.js edit for 3A + H

Two leftovers live there: the card editor's budget table headers and notes still print 'f x ((2A+H) x m + S)' (the numbers come from the shared budget, so they are right), and FORGE_MEAN_GAIN (the enemy's level for a Forge gain) no longer matches the cards (tests/forge-curve check 3; it was already off before BUDGET2).

items.title: PRO decks: leaders and fields to re-bake after BUDGET2
items.body: Two BUDGET2 changes reach canonical/pro-skirmishes.json, which this package was not allowed to edit. (1) The re-fit moved the stats that pick a PRO deck's showcase leader (rarity, then Attack + Health / 2): 4 maps' DECK1 decks (mu, mn, mk, mt) and 6 PRO decks (7-PRO-2, 7-PRO-4, 8-A-PRO-1, 9-PRO-2, 16-PRO-1, 16-PRO-4) now name a different leader than the game would pick (tests/deck1 4 checks, tests/pro 6). (2) The sims now see the map's biome flags (hotMap, coldMap, saltMap, weatherMap), so 15 maps' stored 'average field' lacks flags the game's own fights carry (tests/pro check 1): a PRO fight on a hot, cold, salt or dry map plays without its Heat / Frost / Salt / Drought skills. The decks themselves were searched under the old stats.
options: Re-bake leaders and fields only (DECK1's tool, no new search)
Re-run DECK1's searches on the new cards (Maps 0-20, about the DECK1 cost)
Leave until the next balance pass
items.default: Re-bake leaders and fields only (DECK1's tool, no new search)
items.outcome: Coordinator (owner's standing 'fill in the decisions'): yes, re-bake the PRO leaders and stored fields, after SKILL2's re-pricing (with DECK1-2).

items.title: New skill Relict: what does it do?
items.body: Owner 10-31 10:17: "New skill Relict - (ill think about what it does. For now out in idea decisions, not gameplay decisions tab)". A relict is a species surviving from an older age (ties in with the Map 40+ Relic discovery: fossils and remnants back into cards). Not built; waiting for the owner's idea. Suggestions (2026-11-02, owner asked 19:56): a) Unbothered by the age: a Relict ignores the map's field effects (weather, time of day, terrain, wind), good and bad. Simple, reads at a glance, and every map now has its own field (ENG16). b) Fossil: when a Relict dies it leaves a Fossil in its slot (a 0/3 wall); at Map 40+ a Relic discovery can wake a Fossil back into the card at Level 1. c) Old blood: a Relict cannot be lowered below its printed Attack and Health (no debuffs, shrink or Decay below its base). d) Living record: +1/+1 for each other Relict you have played this fight (a small tribe). Recommended: a) now, b) when Map 40+ Relics are built.
options: c) Cannot be lowered below its printed stats
items.answer: a) Ignores field effects, and also field-level skills (Earthquake and the like, weather changes, everything field-wide); normal skills still affect it. Owner 2026-11-04 22:34: "a. and also general field-level skills like earthquake etc, weather changes etc, everything. Normal skills are fine"

items.title: Should the progression reference's unused Dust go to the Forge?
items.body: REF5 (docs/balance/ref5-2026-10-30.md): the brief splits income x1.5 into 1.0x for packs and 0.5x for levelling. No pack costs Dust, so the 1.0x Dust share (8,775 by Map 20 for seed 1) sits unused, and Dust is what limits the Forge: the Ember Forge is never bought and the decks reach a mean level of 1.8-2.6 from Map 11, against the Map reference's 3-3.9.
options: Keep: 0.5x of every currency for the Forge
items.outcome: Coordinator (owner's standing 'fill in the decisions'): yes, the unused Dust goes to the Forge. Applied in the re-run after BUDGET2.

items.title: Gold Leaves in the progression reference's economy
items.body: REF5: no confirmed reward (first clears, faction / level track, the Trail's free lane) pays Gold Leaves, so the Tidemire Chest (6) and the Highcrest Case (11) are never affordable and every bought pack is a Hedgerow Pouch (Maps 0-6 cards); the Pack 1 pool is full by Map 6, so the 5 seeds' collections hardly differ.
options: Count the S notices and the daily dungeons' Gold Leaves at a stated pace

items.title: The race window: 120 ms
items.body: K12's rule ("If there's ever a race condition, smaller index player takes priority"): every placement is a claim to the room's host; the host gathers the claims that arrive within 120 ms of the first one as one moment and lands them lower player index first, each checked against the board as it stands, so of two claims on one slot player 1's lands and player 2's card goes back to its hand with a note naming who took it. A claim on a slot that already landed is refused whoever made it (no stealing a slot after it shows). A longer window favours player 1 more often; a shorter one follows arrival order more closely.

items.title: CPU allies play first: alongside you, or before you may play?
items.body: W4 ("The allies should play their cards first if CPU btw, taking a random amount of time between 0.5 to 3.0s. (0.5 to 1.5s in the first turn only)"). Built: each CPU ally starts its own timer as the turn begins (0.5-1.5 s on a floor's first turn, 0.5-3.0 s after) and plays when it fires; you may play at the same time, and the round waits for every CPU ally. So if you wait a moment you see its play first; if you are quick you go first. The other reading would lock your hand until every CPU ally has played (up to 3 s each turn).
options: Lock my hand until the CPU allies have played
items.answer: Owner 2026-11-02 19:56: "They play at the random time - that feels natural. If you play before they play, they may recalculate their action before they play it." Alongside (built), plus: a CPU ally whose timer has not fired re-plans after your play (ENG18).

items.title: "Adjacent" includes the card in front of or behind yours
items.body: W10 ("You can also place cards in your allies' rows and vice versa if you have a card adjacent. However you cannot use your allies' 'network' to place cards."). Built: a slot is open to you when one of YOUR cards is beside it in its row, or in the same column one row in front or behind (that is how a card of yours can be next to an ally's row at all), plus your own row's centre. An ally's cards open nothing for you. Units a skill makes count as the player's whose row they stand in.
options: Beside in the row only (then you could never reach an ally's row)
items.answer: Owner 11-02 19:29: "You cannot use your allies' network. So yes, only adjacent slots to your card(s). Players cannot play cards in middle slots of other rows." As built: only your own cards open slots (beside, or in front / behind in the same column); an ally's cards open nothing; another row's centre is never yours (ENG17). Owner 19:56: "Adjacent in front, behind, left, right. Surrounding includes corners."

items.title: Nothing on the board and your centre taken: the slots beside it open
items.body: Owner 11-02 14:26: "this only applies to coop/multiplayer dungeons. Not raids (Raids are always CPU for now)". Owner 11-02 14:10: "only a player can play into the starting card slot of their row. The rest is up for grabs." Each player's row centre (starting slot) is reserved for that player; every other slot is open to either player. Built in ENG17. | With W10's rule an ally (or a CPU ally) who plays into the centre of YOUR row while you have no card on the board would shut you out of the fight. Built: in that case the two slots beside your row's centre are open to you (the normal game's empty-board rule, legalSlots). Otherwise your row's centre is always open to you when it is free.

items.title: The duo dungeon fits the whole match to the window
items.body: Owner 11-02 14:10: OK. ("Vault" is only the code's name for the duo dungeon's battle board.) | W4 ("Why does the duo dungeon start out at such a far away zoom?"). The vault has a full-size row more than a fight (the ally's, now the size of yours: W10), so on a laptop window the hand sat below the fold and the board read as zoomed out. Built: the vault's own middle row (it never plays there) hides while empty, and on a tablet or computer the card size is scaled so the whole match fits the window's height (between 55% and 100%, up to RES3's 145% on a big desktop window); the board starts at 1:1 and zooms out only when units would leave it. At 1366x860 the cards stay 114 px wide (a fight there grows them to 137 px).

items.title: Map card pools: the cap would take 187 cards out of the packs. Which way?
items.body: L7 ("Limit the number of cards in a map ... ~4-5 old cards, ~4-7 new cards"). Today each main map's pool is nearly all of that map's own pack cards (12-26 cards, 0-2 carried from earlier maps). Capped at 7 new and 3-5 old (rewards, first-clear pack cards and showcases always kept), the pools lose 269 entries, and 187 cards (82 Common, 70 Uncommon, 34 Rare, 1 Starter: about a third of the pack cards) are then in no pool, so by the stranding rule they wait for a source and leave the packs. It also invalidates PRO / BPRO decks that hold those cards (235 checks) and puts some trimmed cards over budget (a card with no source counts as Map 0). Nothing is applied; the plan, its before -> after per map and the 187 names are in docs/balance/content4-2026-10-28.md, with a script that applies it. Keeping every card of the maps' PRO decks lowers it to 81 cards waiting, but a dozen maps then stay well over the cap. 2026-10-28: re-opened. Owner 16:43: "balancing this way may make our pack size and unique card total not match." HUB9 (🗺️ Map cards tab) measured the plan: map-listed pack cards would fall to 35/145 (Hedgerow), 61/154 (Tidemire), 49/126 (Highcrest), 26/33 (Pack 4); lists 736 -> 467 entries. Not applied; decide with the tab.
options: Keep the lists as they are
Cap them as planned (cards stay in their packs)

items.title: Shock: 1.5x from every source, or from lightning only?
items.body: L5 built as briefed: a Shocked unit still takes 1.5x from every hit, every source, and Shock is re-priced by the 4-round rule with the card's own chance, rounds and Attack (it was a flat 0.93). By that rule the low-chance cards were about right: the Voltaic Eel's Shock 40%/1 is 0.83 (was 0.93), the Abyss Lantern Squid's 30%/1 1.07, the Electric Catfish's Shock Bolt 2 7.98 (was 6; the Catfish is re-fitted 2/9 -> 2/8). Measured in fights (docs/balance/eng12-uptime-2026-10-28.json) a landed Shock adds about 0.6 (Eel) to 1.3 (Catfish) damage. If Shock still feels too strong, your other idea makes it a lightning combo: Shocked units take 1.5x from lightning only (Electricity, Chain Lightning, Shock Bolt, Thunderstorm, a lightning swing). That would make Shock much weaker and cheaper (about a quarter of its price).

items.title: May a unit woken by a hit swing in that same round?
items.body: L10: the engine never lets an Asleep unit swing (checked over 400 Spore Cloud fights; Ambush and Banana were the two holes, now closed). What your screenshot most likely shows: a hit wakes a sleeper (Sleep's rule), the woken unit then swings in its turn that round, and the replay kept the zZ badge from the round's start. The badge now clears with a 'wakes up' at the hit. Should a woken unit lose the rest of that round instead (it wakes groggy, swings from the next round)?

items.title: Equipment hardiness: Lives on top of durability (Hardy N), and the anti-equipment skills Sunder and Dismantle
items.body: Your 23:58 on OWN-Q2: "Equipment can be destroyed through specific anti-equipment skill. But only at 50% chance ... maybe with armor 'lives' default 1, some have 2-3." Proposal (docs/proposals-2026-10-26.md section 1): durability stays as the wear counter (hit 1, acid 2, Corrode 2; EQ2). New: Lives N (keyword Hardy N, default 1 = today's rule). A break takes one life: durability reaching 0 (then it refills) or a break skill succeeding; at 0 lives the piece is destroyed. Dragonscale Mail Hardy 2; Hardy 3 for a few named Legendary+ metal pieces. Sunder (On Hit: 50% to break the target's piece, 1.0), Dismantle (On Play: 50% to break the facing enemy's piece or a loose one, 0.5), Pulverise breaks a life for sure (+0.5 in its price). Tamper-proof blocks stealing only. A dropped piece keeps lives and wear; the next unit picks it up after Equip Time. Price: equipLifeMult = min(D x L, 4) / 4 + 0.35 for a 2nd life + 0.2 for a 3rd. Shown as gold rings above the durability pips and a gem badge on the card. Also to settle: does Pulverise break for sure or roll 50%?
options: A. Lives on top of durability (recommended)
B. Lives replace durability (only break skills, acid and Corrode take lives, 50% each)
C. Hardy as a quality: immune to break skills, half wear; no lives
items.default: A. Lives on top of durability (recommended)
items.outcome: Owner, 2026-10-26 11:19: "OKAY, Hardy decreases by 1 every break." Build Hardy N on top of durability, -1 Hardy per break.

items.title: The Moon Trail (monthly battle pass) and the packs given for levels
items.body: Your 23:58 on OWN-Q3: "Battlepass is not level locked but gameplay locked. Doing what actions daily or weekly builds up to it. Resets every month." With #51 (25 levels = 25 packs) and B1 / B2. Proposal (docs/proposals-2026-10-26.md section 2): Pawprints from daily notices (10 for D-B, 20 A, 40-100 S-SSS), daily tiers (20/10/10), the first win a day (10), weekly tiers (100/60/40) and three weekly Trail challenges (50 each, from a pool of existing counters plus 4 new ones). 30 tiers at 150 each, reset on the 1st (reached tiers are paid at the reset). Free lane: 6 packs a month (current pack tier x3, faction x2, a Tidemire Chest at 30), Maple Leaves, Dust, 2 Energy capsules, a Raid Ticket, kit items, a monthly title. Premium lane is a locked placeholder (money undecided). Levels: singles at 2-5 and the first pack at 5 as in B1, then a pack only every 5th level (10/15/20/25); the other levels give 100 Maple Leaves + 50 Dust. A full player reaches tier 30 by about day 25, a regular player tier 17. An input for B2's curve: 330 + 30(L-1) + 10(1.06^(L-1) - 1) (Levels 15-25: 9,048 XP instead of 12,765).
options: A. Moon Trail with packs; level packs every 5 levels (recommended)

items.title: Should a PvP stranger's deck be levelled to your battle rating?
items.body: Your G22 question, from the code: PvP is not scaled to your BR. The opponent is a recorded deck (a player's or a seeded stranger) from your Elo tier (6 tiers on the rating curve, widening one tier at a time until at least 6 candidates), drawn at random with a 60% pull toward decks whose battle rating is near yours (weight 0.4 + 0.6 x e^(-|BR difference| / max(8, your BR / 4))). Its cards fight as recorded; nothing is levelled up or down, and the win moves your rating by Elo (K 24). Options: keep it, or level the stranger's cards so its BR matches yours (a fairer fight, but a strong deck no longer reads as strong), or match on BR first and Elo second.

Match on BR first, Elo second

A level here is a Forge level gained over each copy's own starting level, so at Map 0 every card has its printed stats. items.title: The CPU is stronger on Maps 0-20: retune the road after EN8?
items.body: Measured (tools/en8_cpu_pitch_2026_10_24.js, every fight of Maps 0-20 and their side maps as the game builds it, 40 games each, the reference player at Smart): the new-player win rate fell from 76.0% to 64.4% (docs/balance/en8-cpu-pitch-before-all.json -> -after-all.json). Of the ~12 points: the CPU's new pitch about 5.5 (its first card down: round 1.19 -> 1.01 on average; the owner's 4-of-20 case 2.59 -> 1.54), brambles that heal an ally instead of themselves (castleRegen, P24-17) about 3.7 (probe files -nopitch / -nopitch-regen), the lethal guard about 0.6 (-after-noguard), the rest (Rampart's columns, Guardian vs Thorns, Windfall) about 2. Nothing was retuned here. Proposal: the next BAL / road-curve pass re-measures and re-tunes the outliers (tools/skirmish_pass.js curve). PRO3 (2026-10-25) did that pass by the agreed schedule (roadCurveTarget, green = target +/- 8): every fight of Maps 0-20 and their side maps measured (tools/skirmish_pass.js measure, 40 games, 241 fights), then CPU deck swaps only (a card of the map's pool for another, the leader, first-clear card and deck size kept, no Shield or Health change). On the curve: green 68 -> 117, too easy 77 -> 56, too hard 81 -> 53; main-map mean 64.0% -> 67.2% (131 decks changed). Most of the 53 still too hard are decks already made of their map's weakest cards (Map 2, Map 4, Map 11 and Map 20's elites, 2-5, 7-6, 11-7, 20-6, 20-8): a swap cannot reach the target there. Your call: accept as is, or allow the next lever for those (drop copies so a deck shrinks, a lower enemy level or bramble, or a stronger reference deck). Data: docs/balance/pro3-road-check-2026-10-25.md (before / after per fight). Owner, 2026-10-25 17:53 (#27, #32): "Master hub difficulty page will flag them out with high difficulty. PRO is not to change any existing skirmishes - they are for me to evaluate the cards in that map. ... (it might be because of the reference deck. let me fight the reference deck as X-REF where X is the map number." Open part: PRO3 retuned 131 road decks by the agreed curve (card swaps only). Keep those swaps, or revert them and only flag the hard fights in the hub? Owner, 2026-10-25 23:58: "Don't retune yet. We'll see the performance against ref decks". Open: revert PRO3's 131 swaps now, or leave the road as it is and re-measure?

items.title: Stone/Metal versions of the lumber gatherers, and other ways to make Lumber: which to build?
items.body: Owner 21:41: 'Lumberjack - what are the stone and metal variants - simple 2x might be too strong. But what other ways to generate lumber?' Proposal: Stone and Metal are scarcer, so their gatherers are slower, not stronger: Stonecutter 'On Ready: +1 Stone every 2nd round'; Prospector 'On Kill: +1 Metal'; Smelter converts 2 Stone -> 1 Metal at round end. Other Lumber sources: Felling (On Kill: +1 Lumber), Salvage (when one of your Structures dies: +2 Lumber), Windfall field (after a Storm round, both sides +1 Lumber), Scavenger (when an ally dies: +1 Lumber), Coppice (a tree Structure that gives +1 Lumber each round while undamaged), Driftwood tide (at Ebb, +1 Lumber on beach maps).

items.title: The Stone loop: Quarry (1 Lumber -> 1 Stone a turn) or a 2 -> 1 converter?

Caves & Alcoves is the Stone map: its Quarry Mole (Bedrock: Armor while you hold 2+ Stone) and Dynamite Packrat (costs 1 Stone) are there to spend it. Stone counts 2 points to Lumber's 1 in the game's resource worth, so Quarry's 1 : 1 is a profit, which is why a card with it pays 2.5 budget points. The alternative you sketched, "at round end spend 2 Lumber -> 1 Stone", is a new skill (a small engine change) and a loss in points; worth it only if Stone should be scarce.

items.title: Dive in two turns: what it is safe from while aloft or under
items.body: Your 13:12 #3 ("like pokemon"), built: once a fight, at its swing, a diver with an enemy unit in its row rises (a Flyer; a Sprinter leaps the same way) or goes under (a Tide unit without wings) instead of swinging. Until its next swing nothing can find or hit it (swings, shots, bolts, skills aimed at a unit; a Spotter neither) and it can't step in as a Guardian. Its next swing strikes the weakest enemy of its row past Taunt (a Guardian beside the target still steps in) for Attack + N, and it is Exposed that round (no Flying dodge, no Tide evade). Area damage that names no target (a field's hail, a Nova, the tide-spout) and its own Poison / Bleed ticks still reach it, as in the games you described (Earthquake hits Dig in some, not Fly). A diver that can't strike in the next round (frozen, stunned) comes down at that round's end without striking. Keep area damage reaching it, or make it safe from everything?
options: Safe from everything while aloft / under
items.outcome: Owner, 2026-10-25 17:53: "don't build this first." Kept as built (area damage still reaches a diver); no further work now.

items.title: Poison / Bleed on extra hits, and "– poison" shots
items.body: Your 13:12 #5 ("common sense, not too overpowered"), built: a unit's Poison N / Bleed N (with Rabid, Greater Poison, Hemorrhage, Venom Master) ride on every landed hit of its own attack damage: the swing, Frenzy's and Twin Strike's swings, Fork / Trident / Pitchfork prongs and Octolash lashes (these already did), and now Pounce and Ambush (which did not). Cleave's side damage is a spread of the swing (an area, as for Guardian): it carries none. A shot or action (Arrow, Fire Arrow, a Bolt, Missile, Deal damage, Volley, Snipe ...) carries none, unless the card says "– poison" / "– bleed" on it (card text "Arrow 2 – poison"; a box on the Arrow, Missile and Deal damage actions in the card editor, as "– bramble"); it then gives the unit's own N, at least 1. Prices (4-round rule): Pounce / Ambush on a Poison or Bleed card pay 0.33 / 0.3 x the status's price on top (no card has both today); "– poison" on a shot 0.9 x Poison's price at that N (Arrow 2 – poison on a plain unit: +2.7). OK?
items.outcome: Owner, 2026-10-25 17:53: "Cleave and related DOES spread the status. I think arrow is okay. price = your decision." Queued: OWN-E7.

items.title: The state skills' prices and cards (Timbered, Bedrock, Forged, Last Stand)
items.body: Stone and Metal are real counts in a fight (pitching a Stone card, Quarry, the Petrified Tree's Stone, the Ore-Smelter Mole's Metal; Stone / Metal costs spend them), so the skills read them directly. Measured how often each state holds (docs/balance/en5-state-uptime-2026-10-24.json, 2000 CPU fights of random live decks): 3+ Lumber 0.9% of unit-rounds (the CPU spends Lumber as it comes), 2+ Stone 0.5% even with 4 Stone makers (one card makes Stone), 1+ Metal 83% with 4 Metal makers, 0.9% without, the bramble at a third or less 10%. Priced by your 4-round rule x the uptime a deck built for it would have: Timbered {+0/+2} 2 x 0.25 = 0.5, Bedrock {Armor 1} 1.5 x 0.2 = 0.3, Forged {+1/+0} 2 x 0.5 = 1.0, Last Stand {+1/+1} 3 x 0.2 = 0.6 (the robust test read plain Last Stand 0.62, Timbered 0.38). Their braces cost the same uptime x the braces. Cards: Lodge Engineer (Timbered), Quarry Mole (Bedrock), Badger Trench Digger (Last Stand); no Forged card (the only Metal maker, the Ore-Smelter Mole, already has two skills and would hold Forged nearly always).

items.title: Bleed and Poison: the measured curve flattens
items.body: Your BP-1: "price it according to your simulation. Note that bigger numbers make them stronger". tools/skill_test_robust.js --mono --multi, 3000 games a setup, with the units priced at a trial 1 a point so the decks stay off the floor (EN4's 'about 2' for Bleed 2 / Poison 2 came from decks priced at 5.2 that lost 97% of their games). Worth with companions at N 1 / 2 / 3 / 4: Bleed 3.5 / 6.2 / 6.6 / 6.3, Poison 2.9 / 5.7 / 5.9 / 5.4 (docs/balance/en5-bleed-poison-2026-10-24.md). Bigger numbers are stronger in all up to 3, but each point is worth less: the stack outlives the small units it lands on. Priced S(N) = 3.6 x N^0.6 (Bleed) and 3.0 x N^0.7 (Poison), a power curve through N 1-3: Bleed 3.6 / 5.5 / 7.0, Poison 3.0 / 4.9 / 6.5 (was 2.6 / 5.2 / 7.8 for both). So a Bleed 1 or Poison 1 card costs more than before and a Bleed 3+ card less. The actions (Bleed / Poison in triggers) and the family (Gash, Venomous, Rabid ...) are unchanged.
options: Linear at the measured N 2 (Bleed 3.1, Poison 2.8 a point)

items.title: Equipment durability: defaults by rarity, and what it does to the pieces' prices
items.body: Built (package EQ2, from your EQ-1 'Durability with acid / Corrode wear'): every piece has durability, its card's own number or by rarity: Common and Uncommon 3, Rare to Super Rare 4, Epic and up 5. A hit on the wearer takes 1 (a swing, a shot, a bolt, a raid smack, a floor's burn; a Poison or Bleed tick is not a hit), an acid hit 2, each Corrode applied 2. At 0 it breaks: it leaves play and its stats and skills come off the unit (Health never below 1). A dropped or stolen piece keeps its wear. The 50% / acid-death rule you disliked is not used. Price (4-round rule, bramblewood-budget.js equipLifeMult): a piece lasts about its durability in rounds, so it counts min(durability, 4) / 4 of its stats and grant: x0.75 for the Common and Uncommon pieces, x1 from Rare. All ten pieces were already well under N; durability frees 0.6-2 points on the five Common / Uncommon ones (docs/balance/eq2-equipment-2026-10-24.json). No card was changed.

items.title: Dive: the simplest form (once a fight, the weakest unit of the row, no landing move)
items.body: Built (package EQ2, N21-5; your note: a diving flier is 'exposed', no 50% miss advantage while diving). From docs/ramming-proposal-2026-10-21.md option C, cut to its simplest: Dive N (N 1 by default): once a fight, the unit's swing goes to the weakest enemy unit (least Health, the nearest on a tie) in the row it faces, past any Taunt, for N more damage. A Guardian beside that unit still steps in. It does not move: no landing in the target's column. A diving Flyer is exposed for the rest of that round: attacks at it get no Flying dodge. Only a Flyer, a Tide unit or a Sprinter can have it (diveEligible). Priced 0.75 a point by the 4-round rule (N once = 0.5 N, the pick of the weakest +0.5, the exposure -0.25). No card has it yet.

items.title: Parasite as built, and the Clinging Leech
items.body: Your 10-21 note (docs/titles-transforms-2026-10-21.md): 'Hooks onto enemy units? Not just leech-attacking from our side. So you place onto an enemy such that their column would be in reach.' The rest was undefined, so package EQ2 proposed and built: a Parasite card may be played onto an enemy unit in your reach (the centre, or a column with or beside one of your units) instead of into your slot (it may still be played as a plain unit). It rides its host: no slot, blocks nothing, can't be hit. It waits its own Wait, then feeds as each round's fight begins: its Attack as a flat hit on the host (no dodge, no Armor, no Guardian), healing itself as much. One Parasite a host, never on a Structure. When the host dies it drops onto your side in that column if the slot is free, else into your graveyard. Priced 1 (the sure hit and the safety against no lane blocked and no bramble damage). The CPU hooks it onto the enemy in reach worth the most. New card: Clinging Leech (Uncommon, 1 Lumber, Wait 1, 4/9 by the budget, placeholder art), awaiting a source.

items.title: The Ambush: what stays locked, and until when
items.body: Built from 'Those ambush skirmishes should lock the previous path I was going for. But then they also shouldn't be connected by a link but instead float there. The moment they are observed (ambushed), they are permanently accessible': the Ambush has no trail to or from it and floats where the scout shoved you; it is open the moment it is seen and stays on the map for good, won or not. items.title: How Greater Poison ticks
items.body: Your 22:23 #7: "when units are hit with Greater Poison - all existing poison is converted to greater poison. Greater poison only hits for 1 poison by default. Usually they have both GP and Poison." Built: Greater Poison N (N 1 by default) on the attacker; its swing that gets through turns ALL the Poison the target had before the hit into Greater Poison and adds N; the swing's own Poison then lands as plain Poison, for its next hit to turn. The status: (A, built) each stack deals 2 a round, then the stack loses 1, as Poison does: Poison twice over. Poison 3 deals 3+2+1 = 6; turned, 6+4+2 = 12. (B) its whole stack every round, never wearing off: that is Toxin, which the game already has, so B would make Greater Poison 'Poison that turns into Toxin'. (C) its stack every round, wearing off 1 every 2 rounds. A reads plainest and keeps Toxin its own thing. Cure takes Poison first, then Greater Poison; Poison Tick (Venom Pulse) ticks both; Hunter (Poisoned) counts it. Status pip: a violet 💀 beside the green ☠.
options: (B) its stack every round, never wears off (as Toxin)
(C) its stack every round, -1 every 2 rounds

items.title: Use the optimizer's Elo gap as the difficulty dial for skirmish decks?
items.body: The optimizer measures how far each fight deck sits below the best deck its map's cards can make (Elo = 400 log10(p / (1 - p)) of the optimum's fair head-to-head score; +200 = the optimum wins 76%, +400 = 91%). Today the Map 0-2 fight decks sit about 300-750 Elo below the optimum, and the gap does not fall steadily along a map. Proposal: give each fight a gap target that falls from about 600 (first skirmish) to about 150 (the map's boss), and toward 0 by Map 20; tune decks to it with the tool, and keep the level, bramble and field levers for the rest.

items.title: Bleed now fades at the round's end, after it bleeds
items.body: Your 19:27 #5: "before they TAKE the bleed or poison damage, they -1. They should take the damage first." Bleed lost its stack at each round's START (since 10-18), before the unit acted, so a Bleed 3 dealt 2 then 1 (3 in all) instead of 3, 2, 1 (6). Built: a Bleeding unit loses 1 stack at the END of a round in which it started Bleeding or bled; a stack that lands after its last action that round waits for the next round's end, so it is bled in full first. A Waiting unit (which can't bleed on its own actions) still loses 1 a round from its second round. Festering still holds it. The grey drop plays at the round's end. Poison was already right in the engine (the tick is the whole stack, then -1); the board showed the badge drop at the same instant as the damage, so it now drops about half a second after the damage. Card-matrix results change wherever Bleed is in play (see the CHANGELOG).

Only after it bleeds (no wear-down at all while it can't act)
Round's end for every stack, late ones too (simpler, a late stack loses 1 unbled)
items.default: As built (round's end, after it bled; a late stack waits a round)

items.title: Shore Up, the opposite of hunkering down: three ideas (not built)
items.body: Your 19:27 #4: "New Skill: Shore Up, opposite of Hunker Down? What could they do?" There is no Hunker Down skill; the nearest is Cower (hit last turn: it hides in its shell or backs off, no attack) and Shell. Three ways to turn that round: (A) SHORE UP N, the mason: each hit it survives, its bramble gets N Health back (On Attacked 1.9 x Rebuild 0.2 a point = about 0.4 per N); it fights on, and the beating it takes props up the bramble. (B) SHORE UP, brace the line: when it is hit (and survives) it doesn't hide; the allies beside it get Shield 1 for the next round (On Attacked 1.9 x Shield 0.35 x 2 allies = about 1.3); Cower saves itself, this saves its neighbours. (C) SHORE UP N, dig in when left alone: at the start of a round after one in which nothing hit it, it gains Shield N, up to 2N (On Round Start 3.5 x Shield 0.35 x about half the rounds = about 0.6 per N); Cower fires after a hit, this after a quiet round. Prices are estimates from canonical/skill-costs.json; each would be measured with tools/skill_test_robust.js once built.

It is what puts the standard pattern inside your window (tools/rw5_faction_pacing_2026_10_23.js, median of 20 seeds): otters first Rare Map 14, last standard Uncommon Map 15, no Very Rare by Map 24; hummingbirds first Rare Map 14, last standard Uncommon Map 16, no Very Rare by Map 24. items.title: Climbing the rarity tree: the pattern moves up once you hold 2 of each of your side's cards (1 of the other side's)
items.body: Your rule "pool copies = the most a deck may hold" makes a big pool: as the game builds it, 60 cards / 204 copies (110 common, 59 uncommon, 26 rare, 4 veryrare, 1 epic, 1 high, 1 superrare, 2 heroic). If the pattern only climbed when a rarity's copies ran out, Uncommons would still come at Map 24 (too many). Built (FACTION_CLIMB_HOLD, from "you will slowly get 1-2x of each copy along the way, climbing the rarity tree"): a rarity is done for the pattern once you hold 2 copies of each of its cards of your side and the shared ones and 1 of the other side's and of each Base card; the rest of the copies stay in the pool for the random faction rewards. Note: the hub counts 30 faction cards as unplaced because they carry the old `unattainable` flag, but the game no longer reads it (obtainability comes from the source), so they are in the pool and in faction rewards today. With only the released 26 cards the pool runs dry around Map 17-19.

items.title: Fighting in the middle: a CPU lane preference (built), or a rule
items.body: Your 13:16 #2 / #11. Measured (tests/en2-cpu-side-sim-2026-10-23.js, Maps 0-5 skirmishes, 840 games a level; docs/balance/en2-cpu-side-*.json): the basic and smart CPUs had no left lean (37.7% left, 38.1% right of their units); the smartest leaned left (40.8% / 33.3%) because its ties always went left. Against a player who builds on one edge, the basic CPU already puts 54% of its units on that side. Built (modest): when the CPU has no kill or trade to make, its random slot is weighted to the middle three slots and to slots facing or beside your units; the smartest CPU gets a small middle bonus and breaks ties toward your units, else a coin. Result: the smartest's lean is gone (mean slot -0.18 -> +0.01), contested placements +1.5 to +3 points, the CPU's win rate down about 2 points. A stronger push would have to be a rule both sides feel, e.g. +1 Attack for units in the middle three slots, or the bramble taking half from the outer lanes.

items.title: How should equipment be damaged or removed: durability worn by hits and acid (recommended), or another design?
items.body: Owner (10-23 11:11): "New: How to deal damage to equipment. (They do not have 'health stats'.) If the opponent has many equipment on the field, they act as perma buffs (albeit activating only 1 turn later). I don't think this rule is fun: 'When an equipped creature dies, the equipment has 50% chance to be destroyed. If defeated by acid damage, the equipment is 100% destroyed'" The rule today (bramblewood-engine.js, eqDrop, package EQ 10-19): the quoted 50% / acid rule is not in the engine or the texts. When the wearer dies, the piece stays in its slot and the next unit played there picks it up (Codex: "it stays when its unit dies"). It goes to the graveyard only if its card has equip.breaks, or if the slot already holds a loose piece. A reviving unit keeps its piece. A loose piece cannot be hit (swings pass it to the bramble). The only answer is Disarm (Glintsnatch Magpie), which steals a piece. So equipment is close to a permanent buff, as you say. Alternatives. (A) Durability: each piece has 2-4 durability pips. It loses 1 each time its wearer takes a hit (or, for weapons, each swing) and breaks at 0. A dropped piece keeps its pips. Pros: no randomness, hitting the wearer is the counterplay, readable. Cons: a new number on every equipment card and in the budget. (B) Corrosion: acid hits and Corrode strip durability (or destroy a loose piece outright), and fire burns wooden pieces. Pros: gives acid its own job and uses existing statuses. Cons: alone it answers equipment only for acid decks. (C) A Sunder family next to Disarm: Sunder N (On Hit: the target's piece loses N durability, or breaks if it has none), Shatter (On Play: break the nearest loose enemy piece), and Demolisher also hits loose pieces. Pros: a deck-building answer. Cons: if few cards carry it, pieces stay permanent buffs. (D) Pieces drop and rust: when the wearer dies, the piece lies loose for 2 rounds, then rusts away unless a unit of its side picks it up; the killer's Disarm or Scavenge can claim it. Pros: keeps the drop-and-pick-up idea, ends permanent buffs. Cons: a timer to show on the board. Recommended: A with B folded in. Durability 3 by default (set per card), -1 each time the wearer is hit, -2 for an acid hit or each Corrode applied; dropped pieces keep their durability. Add C's Sunder to a few cards later.
options: Pieces drop and rust after 2 rounds (D)
Break on the wearer's death (equip.breaks for all)

items.title: Deck slot prices
items.body: Built (UI4, your 01:03 note 5): a new player has 1 deck slot; more are bought in order in the Camp (under My Decks) or the Tavern's Upgrades tab. Slot 2: 150 Magic Dust + 150 Maple Leaves. Slot 3: 300 Dust + 250 Leaves. Slot 4 (Map 15 cleared): 600 Dust + 350 Leaves + 1 River Pearl + 1 Tempering Stone (Map 15's boss pays both on its first clear). Slot 5 (Map 21 cleared): 900 Dust + 450 Leaves + 1 Ember Core (from the Map 20 raid / world bosses). Slot 6 (Map 27): 1200 + 600 + 2 Ember Cores. Slot 7 (Map 33): 1500 + 750 + 1 Strange Materia + 1 Ember Core. Maps 27 and 33 are still Reserved, so slots 6-7 wait for them. Map 21's own fights pay only Iron Shards, so slot 5 asks for the Ember Core the road pays just before it. Existing saves keep every deck they have (their slots start at their deck count); a deck pulled from the cloud raises the slots the same way.

The engine's Swarm counts the OTHER allies that share a type, so an Ant Scout (1 Attack) with 3 ants out shows 1 + 3 = 4; your example said 1 + (3+1) x 1 = 5, which would count the scout itself. items.title: Difficulty doesn't climb: from Map 16 the road gets easier, not harder
items.body: Measured on all 179 fights of Maps 0-24 (docs/balance/df-2026-10-23.json): the road gets easier from Map 16, not harder. The ant deck wins 64-74% of skirmishes on Maps 0-15 but 88-96% on Maps 16-24; a collected deck 81%. Causes: your level climbs 1 -> 8 between Maps 10 and 16 while the enemy's climbs 2 -> 3.2; the level curve is stepped; and every map's targets restart at 90% -> 40%. A trial 'pace' curve (the enemy 0.5-2.5 levels under your Forge cap) lowers Maps 16-24 skirmishes to 88% (ant) / 73% (collected). Recommended: the pace curve, plus DF-3's boons, plus targets that drift down across maps (first skirmish 90% on Map 1 to about 80% on Map 24), retuned against the ant and collected decks.
options: The pace enemy curve, plus DF-3's selfish effects, plus road targets that drift down across maps (each map's first skirmish 90% on Map 1 to about 80% on Map 24), retuned against the ant and collected decks
No level change: get the climb from DF-3 and from retuning each fight against the ant and collected decks
items.default: The pace enemy curve, plus DF-3's selfish effects, plus road targets that drift down across maps (each map's first skirmish 90% on Map 1 to about 80% on Map 24), retuned against the ant and collected decks
items.outcome: Owner (10-23 17:34): "Ill evaluate this when my new account progresses to that point. Map MUST absolutely contribute at 0.2* per Map. In the backend, I think you define Map as the reward source. But for Pack rewards - what source do you select? If its a Pack reward, select the first Map it appears (along the main line, not submaps). 20*0.2=4, a reasonable bonus. This may be enough to balance stronger maps and also make them appealing." Two rules for the stat budget: (1) the Map term is 0.2 per map (bramblewood-budget.js has perMap 0.1 since BF6 halved the coefficients, so it goes back to 0.2: a Map 20 card gets +4 N); (2) a pack card's map is the first main-line map it appears on, never a submap (today cardObtainMap uses the map where its pack goes on sale). New work: a balance package sets perMap 0.2, changes the pack rule in cardObtainMap, regenerates canonical/card-obtain-maps.json and re-fits the cards (docs/action-items.md, 10-23 17:34). Which climb fix goes in (the pace curve or another option) waits for his own play-through: DF-1b.
items.buildNote: Built by BAL2 (2026-10-24): perMap 0.2 (bramblewood-budget.js, canonical/skill-costs.json). "Appears on" is read as OBTAINABLE on that main-line map, as a reward or out of a pack there: a basic-pack card counts from the earlier of its pool map (the base track and the card drop; a side map at the main map that unlocks it) and the first main map that pays its pack (the end-of-map packs: Pack 1 Map 0, Pack 2 Map 7, Pack 3 Map 14), never before its rarity reveals on the main road (rarityIntroMap now reads ROAD_MAIN_FROM: Epic 22, Heroic 25); a map reward counts at the main map that unlocks its map. So Pack 1 cards count as Map 0 (they come out of Map 0's end pack), Pack 2 as Map 7, Pack 3 as Map 14: 339 cards' map moved down, 17 up, and with the doubled coefficient most map cards gained N. canonical/card-obtain-maps.json regenerated. Re-fit (tools/bal2_refit_2026_10_24.js): 254 cards on their old line rose to the new one, 36 over the new budget went down, 10 cuts over 25% held at their stats (alley-cat, honey-badger-fury, chipmunk-hoarder, chipmunk-cavalry, pyroclast-wyrm, plague-gnat-cloud, sunfeather-scout, lone-grey-wolf, rock-pool-starfish, muskrat-lodgekeeper) and 15 with no legal line kept; both lists merged into docs/balance/human-pass-1-flagged-2026-10-21.json. docs/balance/bal2-refit-2026-10-24.json lists every move.

items.title: When your new account reaches Maps 16-24: does the road still get easier, and which climb fix goes in?
items.body: Split from DF-1 (DC3). Owner (10-23 17:34): "Ill evaluate this when my new account progresses to that point." Measured (docs/balance/df-2026-10-23.json): the ant deck wins 64-74% of skirmishes on Maps 0-15 but 88-96% on Maps 16-24, because the player's level climbs 1 -> 8 between Maps 10 and 16 while the enemy's climbs 2 -> 3.2. DF-2 (Base cards stop at Lv 4) and DF-3 (selfish boons from Map 5) are approved and change the curve; DF-1's Map rule (0.2 per map, pack cards from their first main-line map) is recorded on DF-1. Left for his play-through: whether the enemy's levels also follow a 'pace' curve (0.5-2.5 levels under your Forge cap), with road targets that drift down across maps (first skirmish 90% on Map 1 to about 80% on Map 24).
options: The pace enemy curve plus drifting road targets (recommended)
No level change: DF-2, DF-3 and per-fight retunes are enough
items.default: The pace enemy curve plus drifting road targets (recommended)
items.outcome: Owner, 2026-10-25 17:53: "road should ROUGHLY always get harder. we can't always achieve this. at the most, we hope to be roughly AS difficult as the previous map while teaching something. I would say, as long the error bars are about +-5% for 1 sigma, that's actually ideal. +10% is acceptable. +15% is less liked, but okay. +-20% is starting to be unacceptable" Recorded as the road tolerance in docs/evaluation-protocol.md.

items.title: Levels gate by map, not by resources; Base decks never need replacing
items.body: Model in docs/balance/df-2026-10-23.json: every deck reaches the Forge cap on the map that opens it (Lv 3 at Map 11, Lv 8 at Map 16), light or binge player alike, so levels gate by map, not by resources. What holds decks back is duplicates outside Base (about 56 repeat fights for one more copy of a common), so the strongest deck is a cheap Base synergy deck that never needs replacing. Recommended: Base cards stop at Lv 4 and pay full Forge cost; a fight's own first-clear card drops 10% a repeat, so 4-copy decks form by about Maps 10-15.
options: Base cards stop at Lv 4 and pay full Forge cost (x1); a fight's own first-clear card drops 10% a repeat (was 3% x its rarity share), so 4-copy decks form by about Map 10-15
Base cards stop at Lv 4 only
Slow the Forge instead: the Ember Forge (Map 16) caps at Lv 6, Lv 8 from Map 21
items.default: Base cards stop at Lv 4 and pay full Forge cost (x1); a fight's own first-clear card drops 10% a repeat (was 3% x its rarity share), so 4-copy decks form by about Map 10-15
items.outcome: Owner (10-23 17:34): "DF-2 OKAY. But of course, don't look down on the grind they have to do to level up their cards to that tier's gate." The recommended option: Base cards stop at Lv 4 and pay the full Forge cost (x1), and a fight's own first-clear card drops 10% a repeat (was 3% x its rarity share), so 4-copy decks form by about Maps 10-15. His note: the model and the tuning must count the grind it takes to level cards up to each tier's gate, not treat reaching it as free. New work: a balance package (docs/action-items.md, 10-23 17:34).
items.buildNote: Built by BAL2 (2026-10-24): Base cards (source Base, starters, tutorial and basic cards) stop at Lv 4 (BASE_CARD_LEVEL_CAP: the Forge, the boss growth, no limit break or Prestige; the Forge says so) and pay x1 (canonical/upgrade-costs.json modifiers.base; quest and map cards keep x0.5); the reference player's Base cards stop at Lv 4 too. A skirmish's own first-clear card drops 10% of its repeat wins, any rarity (SKIRMISH_OWN_REPEAT_DROP), else the pack card at the plain 1%. Elites keep their tier drop (the own-card roll is a skirmish's, as GD built it). The grind to each gate: docs/progression-plan.md (tools/bal2_grind_2026_10_24.js).

items.title: Selfish map effects from Map 5: a boon only the enemy's deck can use

It counts only the CPU's deck, so copying the deck gains nothing. The Environment card shows the count ('11/16 Cave', red outline, a 'theirs' mark). 15 boons are proposed (e.g. Map 8 Blind Fury: Cave units deal 2x in Darkness; Map 17 Frostborn; Map 24 Royal Treasury); Maps 6, 11, 14, 15 and 21 get none. The full list is in this item's earlier text (git history of docs/decisions.json, 10-23). Recommended: build it on every fight of those maps, then retune the road.

Only on elites, mini-bosses and bosses
On skirmishes too, but only from Map 10

Build it: one selfish boon per map from Map 5 (the 15 proposed; Maps 6, 11, 14, 15 and 21 none), on every fight of that map, on when at least half the enemy deck shares the theme; the Environment card shows the count. items.title: A unit at 0 Health before its action ends
items.body: Item 4. A 3/7 Armor 1 Beetle Grunt hit 4, 4, 2 shows 3, 3, 1 and dies at exactly 0; in 13 auto-played 0-4 fights the shown Health matched the engine after every hit and round and every death played at 0 (screens in docs/screens/PG; the final hit shows its number and Health 0 together). One gap with your rule: inside the same action a unit at 0 can't be healed (applyHeal refuses 0 Health), and its On Attacked / Bleed-on-defend don't fire. Should a heal or shield that lands later in the same action save it?

A heal later in the same action saves it

items.body: Built as Spellshield 🪬 (engine key spellshield): a single-target enemy skill (an arrow or other shot, a Bolt, a damage or status skill) aimed at a unit adjacent to it hits it instead; never itself; several at random. Price 0.8 in canonical/skill-costs.json, an estimate (about 3/4 of Guardian's 1.06: fewer hits come as skills than as swings, but they are the heavier ones). items.title: Seven maps have no skirmish-exclusive card
items.body: Maps 4, 6, 11, 12, 18, 20 and 21 have no skirmish whose first clear pays an exclusive card: their own cards sit on their elites and bosses, or are their pack cards. Left as they are ("if it turns out there is not much left, then okay"); their skirmishes pay pack cards. Giving each one would move one of its pack cards (or an elite's card) to a skirmish.

Not the default: on Maps 4, 6, 11, 12, 18, 20 and 21 one pack card moves to a skirmish as its first-clear exclusive card. To build in package RW3. Built (RW3): every main map has a skirmish-exclusive card now. Maps 4, 6, 11, 12, 18, 20, 21 had none: 1 card moved out of the packs on the maps with fewer than 4 skirmishes (Maps 4, 21), 2 on the others (12 cards: snapstick-turtle 4-1; poison-dart-croaker 6-1, booming-bittern 6-2; alpine-marmot 11-1, eagle-owl-quartermaster 11-2; bramble-hoglet 12-1, cunning-vixen 12-2; thorny-devil 18-1, caustic-scorpion 18-2; pack-mule 20-1, ash-cloud-condor 20-2; pika-hoarder 21-1), each from that skirmish's own deck (tools/rw3_first_rewards_2026_10_23.js). Exclusive skirmishes 23 -> 36 (with the Quarry Mole on 8-1, RP3).

items.body: Pack rewards on skirmishes stay as they were (Map 0's 0-2 faction pack; the map free packs are on bosses). Adding packs or Faction Reward tokens to skirmishes would speed up the economy and the faction track, both tuned. 33 of the 101 skirmishes pay no card.

To build in package RW3. Built (RW3): no skirmish pays nothing on its first clear: 101 main-map skirmishes = 36 exclusive cards, 64 cards of that map's pack, 1 pack (0-2's faction pack); was 23 / 44 / 1 / 33 nothing. Every map still had pack cards to give, so no new season or faction pack was needed; the fallback (that season's pack, then your faction pack, taking turns) is built (SKIRMISH_FIRST_PACKS) and empty.

items.title: What reads "adjacent" and what keeps its shape
items.body: On adjacent (in front / behind too, in a raid): Guardian, Spellshield, Formation, Haste, Shieldwall, Amplifier, Immolation, Irradiated, Inspiring, Friction, Proliferate, Electricity, Chain Lightning, Dragon Lightning, Spitfire's splash, the Adjacent Ally target. Kept as they are: shapes across the board (Fireball's 3 columns, Meteor, Rocket, Dynamite's 3x3, Cleave, the prongs, Taunt, Stench, Landslide, Ambush / Sentry facing), where a token appears (Twin, Sprout, Brood, Palisade, Spawner: a free slot nearby), and Pack chains (front row only today).
items.outcome: Owner (10-23 00:10): "Okay. Dynamite is adjacent but including diagonals - is there a way to name this?" Keep the shapes as built (the default). Open naming question: Dynamite reaches the 8 cells around its target, diagonals included; EN proposes one word for it (suggested "Surrounding": left, right, in front, behind and the four diagonals) and uses it in the texts, leaving "adjacent" at the four directions. To build in package EN. Built (EN): the word is "Surrounding": the 8 places around a unit (left, right, in front, behind and the 4 diagonals; in a raid its own rows in front and behind too). A Codex term beside Adjacent. Skills of that shape, now worded with it: Dynamite ("to every surrounding unit"; on the raid board it now also reaches its own rows in front and behind, diagonals included), Scavenge and Salvage. Adjacent stays the four directions. Owner (10-23 11:11): "Adjacent - Up/Down/Left/Right; Surrounding - include diagonals -> Okay!" Confirmed as built.

items.title: An Easter egg a player owns shows as a plain card
items.body: Outside Admin Mode nobody sees an Easter egg: no "???" slot, no section, no count, no filter or search hit, no Easter-egg words. A player who owns one anyway (only an admin grant gives one) sees it in their Codex as an ordinary card, its where-to-get line "Not obtainable yet".
options: Hide it from its owner too
items.outcome: Owner (10-23 00:10): "Yes. The method to own one is in giveaways or supremely low chance in mystery packs" An owner keeps seeing the Easter egg as an ordinary card (the default); what is new is how a player can own one: giveaways, or a supremely low chance in mystery packs. To build in package RW3. Built (RW3): a Mystery Booster card is an Easter egg 0.05% of the time (1 in 2,000 cards; MYSTERY_EGG_CHANCE), one of the nine at random, granted through its own source 'mysteryEgg'. Giveaways are the admin grants that already existed.

items.title: Guardian's front / behind is raid-board only
items.body: In front / behind needs rows that fight, so it applies on the raid board (3 rows, every row acts). Elsewhere a reserve row is only waiting to step up (not on the battlefield), so a Guardian waiting there doesn't guard the unit in front of it, and nothing guards a waiting unit. Normal fights have one row, so they only have left / right (the card matrix shows 0 changed fights); in 600 random raid-board fights with Guardians, 508 ended differently.
items.outcome: Owner 19:27: "GD-1: From now on, things that deal with L/R can just say 'adjacent' e.g. Formation cares about adjacent units. Adjacent is defined as behind, in front, left, right. Only relevant in raids or multi-player dungeons. (I see that Guardian's short desc is already correct)" Built (package GD2): one engine helper, adjacentOf (bramblewood-engine.js): left and right in a unit's own row, plus directly in front / behind only where every row fights (the raid board, RESERVE_ACTS); elsewhere just left / right, so ordinary fights play exactly as before. On it: Guardian, the new Spellshield, Formation (a waiting reserve no longer counts), Haste, Shieldwall, Amplifier, Immolation, Irradiated, Inspiring, Friction, Proliferate, Electricity, Chain Lightning, Dragon Lightning, Spitfire's splash and a trigger's Adjacent Ally target. Their texts and the Codex term say "adjacent" (12 packs). Column shapes keep their columns (call GD2-5). Owner (10-23 11:11): "Adjacent - Up/Down/Left/Right; Surrounding - include diagonals -> Okay!" Confirmed as built.

items.title: Which Guardian steps in: left, right, in front, behind
items.body: When two or more Guardians are next to the target, the first in this order takes the hit: left, right, the one in front, the one behind (the old rule was left before right). A Guardian never guards itself, but a Guardian next to another Guardian is guarded by it.
options: As built (left, right, in front, behind)
In front first (it stands between the enemy and the target)
items.default: As built (left, right, in front, behind)
items.outcome: Owner 19:27: "GD-2: Random," Built (package GD2): when two or more Guardians are adjacent to the target, one of them takes the hit at random (the fight's seeded RNG, so replays repeat; it only rolls with two or more, so a fight with one Guardian draws the same numbers as before).

items.title: Status-only skills still go to the unit they aim at
items.body: Guardian takes single-target hits: a swing, an arrow or another shot, and a skill that deals damage to one target. A skill that only puts a status on one enemy (Poison, Expose, Stun, Bleed or Add Wait aimed at one unit) is not redirected, as before. Area hits are never redirected.
options: A Guardian also takes single-target statuses
items.outcome: Owner 19:27: "GD-3: AOE can't get redirected. Status only skills hmm. I think if it's skills (including arrow), guardianship doesn't help. So no redirection for skills. We have ward for dodging skills right? There can be a similar skill - but for shielding allies from skills." Built (package GD2): Guardian redirects plain swings only: a unit's basic attack and the prongs of that swing (Fork, Trident, Pitchfork, Octolash: each prong is a full single-target swing). Cleave's side damage is a spread of the swing, so not redirected, as before (call GD2-2). Arrows (Arrow, Archer, Snipe), Bolts, shots, damage and status skills reach their target; areas never redirect. New skill Spellshield 🪬 (call GD2-1 for the name): a single-target enemy skill aimed at an adjacent ally hits the Spellshield unit instead. There is no Ward that dodges skills in the game: the closest are Helmet (deflects half the shots aimed at it) and Evasive.

items.title: 💥 is the crit mark; the hit burst keeps 💥
items.body: On numbers and log lines 💥 now means a crit only: Explode's fuse line and its "Boom!" float use 💣, Stampede's log line and its carry-over preview (+N) use 🐘. The quick burst that flashes on a card when it's hit by a physical attack is still a 💥, with no number on it (elemental hits show their own glyph). The raid smack's log line ("💥 X sweeps your front row"), "💥 Crash!" and "👑💥 King Slayer!" keep theirs (words, not a number).
options: Change the hit burst too (e.g. a white spark)
Change every other 💥 in the battle
items.outcome: Owner 19:27: "GD-4: King Slayer: 🗡️, Fencer: 🤺" Built (package GD2): King Slayer's float is "🗡️ King Slayer! +N" (was 👑💥); a Fencing unit's plain hit bursts as 🤺 instead of 💥 (Fencing had no float or log mark of its own; the hit burst was its 💥).

items.title: Skirmishes whose first clear is a pack or a token: 7%
items.body: Every first-clear reward card a skirmish pays today is skirmish-only (since RP, a map's reward cards are never pack cards), so the tripled drop covers those skirmishes. A skirmish whose first clear gives a pack or a Faction Reward / Growth token has no single card to drop, so it has the plain 7% pack-card drop on every win (it had none). If a skirmish is ever given a pack card as its reward, the same 21% rule picks it up.
items.outcome: Owner 19:27: "GD-5: No. There should be a mix of 'no first clear card', 'first clear skirmish-exclusive card', 'first clear pack card reward' and of course pack rewards.. Skirmish exclusive makes up 1-2 (max 3). The rest are a mix of the rest. If it turns out there is not much left, then okay." Built (package GD2): a skirmish's first clear can pay a pack card of its own map (SKIRMISH_FIRST_PACK_CARDS, written by tools/gd5_first_cards_2026_10_22.js; the card stays a pack card). The exclusive cards stay where they were (every map had 0-2). The other skirmishes alternate pack card / none: of 101 main-map skirmishes, 23 pay an exclusive card, 44 a pack card (each one from that fight's own deck), 1 a pack (0-2), 33 nothing. A pack-card skirmish drops like an exclusive one: 7% on its first clear, 21% on repeats with that card at its rarity share. Calls GD2-3, GD2-4. docs/balance/gd5-first-cards-2026-10-22.json.

items.title: The drop line shows the reward card's chance per win
items.body: A cleared skirmish's drop line reads, for a Common reward card: (card) 13% · 🃏 8.4%, its chance a win (21% x 60% = 12.6%, rounded as the line rounds above 10%) and the pack card's share. Before the first clear it reads 🃏 7% (the card itself is in the First Clear box).

items.title: How a 1-damage Crushing Depths halves for Swimmers
items.body: Chosen: a halving keeps at least 1, so at 1 damage a Tide unit or Swimmer takes 1 like everyone. Only when both halvings stack (a Swimmer or Tide unit that also resists water) does it round down: 0 at 1 damage. Hail and Lava Spout keep the game's usual Resist rule (half, at least 1), so Resist does nothing against a 1.
options: Keep (at least 1; Swimmer + Water Resist takes 0)
items.default: Keep (at least 1; Swimmer + Water Resist takes 0)
items.outcome: Owner 14:12: "FX-2: we shall do normal rounding. if x < 0.5, 0; else 1. Is this fair? Only round once, when it comes into fruition on the battlefield. Internal calculations should never round. Even when passing numbers between functions. Idk how you code it internally - the first ApplyDamage(X) before damage calculation and etc. then the final real ApplyDamage(Y) which results in a literal ReduceHealth(Y) 1-1 + firing related triggers." Built (package FX2): damage is worked out exactly (Resist, Weakness, Fragile, Sturdy, Ghost / Supreme / Shade / Atheist halves, Shock x1.5, Rage's half, stone, Armor, a row's half share, Bloodlust, half lines, Stagger, the Psychic Dampener, a Swimmer's half in the Crushing Depths) and rounded once, half up, in applyDamage, the one place a unit's Health goes down for a hit (damageHQ for a bramble). So a Swimmer at 1 takes 0.5 -> 1, a water-resistant Swimmer 0.25 -> 0, as this call's default had it; a 3 into Resist now lands 2 (was 1), a 5 lands 3 (was 2). The "at least 1" after a factor or a half is gone (it was a patch for rounding down).

items.title: Skirmishes with a first-clear reward: no card drop, repeats included
items.body: N22-5 gave the pack-card drop to "skirmishes with no pack or card reward", and RW2 keeps that: a skirmish whose first clear pays a card, a reward token or a free pack never drops a card, not even on a repeat win. Before RW2 those skirmishes still had the old 10% enemy-card drop (RW-3 moved every fight to the one pack drop, so they now have none). Elites and bosses drop on every win.
options: They drop on repeat wins only (7%)
items.outcome: Owner 18:20: "RW2-1: Yes. There are two kinds of first-clear drop card reward skirmishes: skirmish-exclusive, or from that map range's pack. ALL skirmishes have a low chance to get a card from the pack. For skirmishes, the chance of getting a card is tripled. But you mostly (50+%) get THAT card. (If it's higher in rarity, then the chance actually decreases - your call. Maybe 60/50/40/25/20/10/5/4/3/2/1..." Built (package GD): every skirmish win, first clear and repeats, rolls the pack-card drop at 7% (a skirmish paying a card, a token or a pack no longer drops nothing). A skirmish with a first-clear reward card rolls 21% on repeat wins; a card that drops there is its reward card with the share for that card's rarity (Common 60%, Uncommon 50%, Rare 40%, Very Rare 25%, Super Rare 20%, Epic 10%, Heroic 5%, Unique 4%, Legendary 3%, Mythic 2%, Ancient and above 1%; special rarities as their tier), else a pack card as usual. So a Common reward card drops 12.6% a repeat win and a Rare one 8.4%. The rank gate stays. A cleared skirmish's drop line shows its reward card (small tile), its chance and its rank emblem, then 🃏 for the pack card's share. The first clear rolls the plain 7% (it pays the card itself). Calls GD-5 and GD-6.
