The rank gate still applies (an elite or boss drop needs an S win).
items.outcome: Owner (10-23 00:10): "No, the drop rate is based on energy use. I think about 1% per energy. But of course, difficult-er skirmishes like elites have 1/2/3/4% higher chance of dropping (only) since elites and above have shields. Ticketed dungeons keep their higher drop rates. Skirmishes might have shields, but they are rather low" Not the default: replaces 7% per Energy tier capped at 25%. A drop is about 1% per Energy spent; elites and above get 1/2/3/4% more (they have shields); ticketed dungeons keep their higher rates. To build in package RW3. Built (RW3): 1% per Energy tier (ENERGY_COST) + a shield bonus by kind: elite / champion / miniboss / dungeon +1%, sub-boss +2%, boss +3%, world / raid boss, megaraid and final boss +4%; no cap. Skirmish 1%, elite 3%, sub-boss 5%, boss 6%, world / raid boss 8%, megaraid / final boss 9%. A skirmish with a first-clear card rolls 3x on repeat wins (3%), then that card's rarity share (Common 60% ...). The ticketed dungeons (the daily dungeons' floors) keep 7% per tier capped at 25% (7%, mini-boss floors 14%). 10,000-roll checks in tests/rw3-2026-10-23.js.

items.title: Skirmish card drops: 7% a win, and the rarity shares by map
items.outcome: Owner (Oct 22): "80/20 and 70/25/5 is fine." Built (package RW2): Maps 10-29 Common 80% / Uncommon 20% (was 75 / 25); Maps 30+ 70 / 25 / 5 unchanged; Maps 0-9 Common only; then the 5% down / 5% up shift. 10,000 rolls (tests/rw2-2026-10-22.js): Map 15 80.0 / 20.0, Map 35 69.7 / 25.1 / 5.2.
items.body: A skirmish with no card reward, no reward token and no free pack drops a pack card 7% of the time (30% below the old 10%). The base rarity: Maps 0–9 Common only; Maps 10–29 Common 75%, Uncommon 25%; Maps 30+ Common 70%, Uncommon 25%, Rare 5%. Then a shift: 5% one rarity down, 5% one up, and an up has a second 5% roll for one more up. The shares are my reading of "Commons from Map 0, Uncommons from Map 10, Rares rarely from Map 30"; they are the table SKIRMISH_DROP_RARITY in arena_app.js. The drop only lands when the win's rank meets the gate for that card's rarity (RW-1), so on Maps 0–19 a win below B gives no drop. 10,000 rolls: Map 5 gives Common 94.8% / Uncommon 4.9% / Rare 0.3% after the shift (only up-shifts exist from Common), Map 15 gives 72.6 / 26.1 / 1.3, Map 35 gives 68.3 / 25.6 / 5.9 / 0.2 Very Rare.
options: Raise the Rare share on Maps 30+
No drop below a certain rank is fine; show it
Drop the rank gate for skirmish drops

items.title: Other fights keep the old card drop (now rank-gated); skirmish drops use the basic pack pool only

A skirmish with a first-clear reward still drops nothing (call RW2-1).
items.body: Elite, boss and the rest keep rollCardDrop as it was (a chance by fight kind, then one of the enemy deck's cards by the rarity table), only now behind the rank gate. The new skirmish drop draws from the basic pack pool (pool 1) cards the player has reached by map (packCardReached); half the time one of the fight's own pack cards of that rarity, else another card of that rarity from the pool, and from the pool directly when the fight has none. The faction pool (11, the otters and hummingbirds) stays on its own reward track and never drops from a skirmish. A rarity with no card in reach steps down until one has.

items.title: The half-miss ×1.5 counts on the stats only; Fragile is ×0.7 on both caps
items.outcome: Owner (pass III answers): "Do your cut. I misread alot of the x1.5 skills and I used a flat number instead actually." On Fragile: "Fragile should be smth like x0.7 (so that you can have more stats!) ... The idea is that things that must be less than N have a x0.7 multiplier!" Built (package BF7) in bramblewood-budget.js capScores: f × ((2A + H) × m + S) ≤ N and f × (A·H × m + S·|S|) ≤ (N/3)², m = 1.5 per half-miss skill on Attack and Health only, f = fragileUse 0.7 for a Fragile card. BF5's fragileMult (N × 0.75) is gone. The game's editor budget panel, the Test Lab, the hub's Budget & stats and Skill costs tabs and every balance tool read it.
items.body: Pass III's formula option: the half-miss ×1.5 was on S too, so a flyer's skills cost half again. Fragile was −8 as a skill and ×0.75 on N, which shrinks N (fewer stats), the opposite of the intent. Mayfly Dancer (Flying, Fragile) re-fits at 2/7; without Fragile it would get 2/4.
options: ×1.5 on the stats only; Fragile ×0.7 on both left sides
Keep ×1.5 on both scores and Fragile on N
items.default: ×1.5 on the stats only; Fragile ×0.7 on both left sides

items.title: The group dungeon is a Coming soon slot
items.body: You asked for group dungeons with live players, recorded in the Daily Dungeon section. There is no co-op dungeon in the game yet (only the D49 design, docs/coop-dungeon-design-2026-10-13.md), so the Daily Dungeons tab now ends with a Group Dungeon slot marked Coming soon. Building it means the netcode in that doc (the Ranked Live host, extended to 2-4 players).
items.outcome: Owner (10-23 00:10): "AR-3 This is a big pass. I like this. Can you launch a big pass for this." Build the co-op dungeon next (the first option), as one large pass. To build in package AR3. Built (AR3): the Group Dungeon, the Hollow Warren (4 floors: the Bat Roost; the Mole Galleries, cave-ins; the Salamander Pools, a cursed centre; the Matriarch's Hall, the Hollow Matriarch and her marked column). The Dungeons tab's Group Dungeon slot is the entrance now (Open a room / Play with CPU allies / Join by code; invites from the friends list), shown to every player past the tutorial while the daily dungeons stay hidden. A room seats 2-4 players (the host A, then C, D, B; 3 players add a CPU ally in B), ready-up, leave, host migration (the next player in seat order takes over; a player who can't run the fight ends the run cleanly), drops played by a CPU ally and reconnects. The fight: the raid's multi-row engine board (a front and a back row a side, 7 columns: each row's left seat, the shared centre, the right seat), simultaneous plans with a 30 s timer (60 s casual), landing A, B, C, D then the dungeon; a shared-cell contest goes to who locked first; one host runs the engine and sends each round's plans; every other player replays them on the same seeded engine (a hash per round checks it; a player out of step mirrors the host's state until the next floor). Rewards per player: each floor's chest (Maple Leaves and Magic Dust), the Matriarch's pick of three of the dungeon's own cards (once a day); 5 Energy per climb, back if no floor is cleared. Online today: 2 players (the live coop_rooms seats a host and one guest); 3-4 online wait for supabase/proposed/20261023_coop_rooms_4p.sql (AR3-6). Local: 2-4 players in tabs of one browser. Solo: you and CPU allies.

items.title: Transform conditions, as read by package TR
items.body: Enraged: "It has Rage" is read as its Rage being on (Rage, below half Health); having the skill would trigger it at once. Matured: N rounds, 2 by default (tf.rounds; the editor doesn't set N yet). Veteran and Matured count rounds survived on the field, at each round's start. Championed: a kill by its own swing or its Counterattack against the unit it fights (a Guardian that takes the hit is the one it fights); kills by Arrow, Pounce or other skills don't count. Gilded: Lumber 1, Stone 2, Metal 3, Gold 5 each, more than 25, checked as the board updates. No card has a transform preset yet.

Cost it using logic." The Hero XP bar has three sections: Battle XP, Materia XP, and a third that takes either; filling the third with Battle XP is 25% less efficient. To build in package SX. Built (SX): each level's need (heroXpToNext) is split in thirds: Battle, Materia, Either. Battle XP fills only the first, Materia XP only the second; the third takes Materia 1:1 and Battle at 75% (HERO_XP_EITHER_BATTLE). A level is gained when all three are full; XP past a full part waits for the next level. The save keeps two pools (xpB, xpM since a base level, lvBase); h.xp stays the plain total. Old saves keep their level and their XP into it becomes Battle XP. The Hero Hall shows the three parts (Either split: Materia violet, Battle striped ember), the rule as the bar's tooltip and as a line under it, each part's numbers on hover. Calls SX-2, SX-3.

items.title: Siding with Otters or Hummingbirds: approve the proposal as written, or answer its questions (a)-(f) first?
items.body: (Rewritten 10-23 at the owner's request, all inside this item; the older siding-proposal-2026-10-08.md is source material, to move into the hub later.) What it is: the player is a traveller both peoples want on their side: the Otters (Rivergate Legion) and the Hummingbirds (Sunfeather Tribes). A hidden Standing number from -100 (Otters) to +100 (Hummingbirds) moves with the player's choices, and the band it sits in decides which rewards, titles, shops and story branches open. Where it lives today: the side picked in the tutorial is stored as `bramblewood_arena_faction` (saveFactionChoice / loadFactionChoice, arena_app.js) and today only sets the starter deck, the voice in warnings and the faction pack; cards carry `faction` (14 Hummingbird cards, 27 base) and `source.side` ('tribes', 'shared'); the faction reward track (noteFactionReceived) counts faction-pack pulls. Dialogue choices already exist (playDialogue with onDone replies, for example the Old Well in visitOldWell). Nothing reads a Standing yet. What siding changes for the player: (1) Reward cards: some skirmishes offer two reward cards, one per side; the player gets the one matching their band, Neutral gets a third (road-folk, dog or cat card). (2) Side shops: a Legion Quartermaster and a Tribe Trader on later maps, different stock. (3) Titles and character looks (Legion Outrider, Friend of the Tribes, Wanderer of Both Banks). (4) Materia leaning: Otter crafting nudges Shield/Formation, Hummingbird crafting Flight/Bond. (5) Story: dialogue warms or cools by band; from Map 6 a key skirmish plays differently by band; a Neutral track keeps the peace through a series of tests, hardest, with unique rewards. (6) It never locks a people's cards away: off-side cards stay in packs and the Market, only the story rewards differ; and nobody is punished for the tutorial pick. What moves Standing: dialogue choices +/-2 to 8 (no number shown on the button), first clears of one people's skirmishes +/-1 (fighting Otters drifts you to the Hummingbirds and the reverse), side quests +/-5 to 15 (a few per map, often exclusive), neutral acts (helping dogs, cats, road-folk, the Traveller) pull toward 0. Drift is slow: 2-3 maps of consistent choices to a friend band, most of the campaign to be Sworn. Five bands: Sworn Otter (<= -60), Otter friend (-59 to -20), Neutral (-19 to 19), Sunfeather friend (20 to 59), Sworn Sunfeather (>= 60); a two-coloured banner on Profile and the Conquest map shows the band. Build in four steps: (1) the Standing store (saved with the account), the banner and hidden weights on dialogue choices, Old Well first; (2) two-sided reward cards on 3-4 skirmishes of Maps 1-3, picked in the skirmish editor; (3) two side quests per map for Maps 1-3; (4) side shops from Map 4, titles, the Map 6 fork. Open questions for you: (a) start at +/-10 from the tutorial pick, or everyone at 0? (b) is the meter shown as a number or only as the band name? (c) is Neutral a full third path with its own ending, or only a resting place? (d) should the two-sided rewards and the side quests wait until the factions are symmetric (RP4), so neither side is the stronger pick? (e) how does siding interact with the Hummingbird gate (the faction pack) and the 0-2 faction pack? (f) can the player reset Standing, or does drift back by effort only? Options stay: Approve as written, Change parts, Not yet. Waiting for your pass over (a)-(f).

items.title: Which AI services should we set up, free tiers first, and will you create the accounts? (your browser; nothing bought)
items.body: Owner (10-23 17:38): "A1 description - list all the AIs that could help us, esp through omnirouting to gain utility without spending tokens." Researched 2026-10-23 (free limits change often; each is re-checked on its own page before use). The idea: send cheap or bulk work (translations, drafts, sim summaries, second-opinion reviews) to free tiers through one router, and keep Claude for design, engine and final review. Every account below is yours to create; Claude never creates accounts, enters passwords or buys anything, and no key goes into the repo or a chat (keys live as local environment variables). ROUTERS (one key, many models). (1) OpenRouter: 20+ ":free" models from several providers behind one OpenAI-style API; 20 requests/min and 50/day free, 1,000/day after a one-time $10 top-up (your call). Account: openrouter.ai. (2) LiteLLM (open source, runs on your machine): one local endpoint that routes to the free tiers below and falls back when one is rate-limited; no account. (3) Vercel AI Gateway: multi-provider with your own keys (BYOK), on the Vercel account you already have. FREE TEXT / CODE MODELS (behind a router). Google AI Studio (Gemini Flash / Flash-Lite and 2.5 Pro free; free-tier prompts may be used by Google to improve its products, fine for this public repo, not for secrets); Groq (about 30/min, 1,000/day; Llama 3.3 70B); Cerebras (about 1M tokens/day); Mistral (about 1B tokens/month, Codestral for code); GitHub Models (150-1,000/day, on your GitHub login); Cloudflare Workers AI; NVIDIA NIM. Use for us: first-draft translations of the 12 language packs, text and lore drafts, summarising sim logs, a second reviewer on diffs. Local and free with no account: Ollama with open models (Qwen, Llama, Gemma) on your own machine. TRANSLATION. DeepL API Free: 500,000 characters a month at no cost (account at deepl.com; it may ask for a card to verify, nothing is charged on Free). Good for checking the language packs against the English. CODE REVIEW. CodeRabbit: free reviews on public repositories with the paid-tier features for open source (sign in with GitHub); CodeQL already scans every push (S4). ART (beside PixelLab and NightCafe, already in use). ChatGPT image generation free daily cap (commercial use allowed by OpenAI's terms); Gemini "Nano Banana" free in the app (visible and invisible SynthID watermark, so drafts only); Ideogram about 10 slow credits/day (free images are public); Leonardo 150 tokens/day (free-tier images not for commercial use); Microsoft Copilot 15 fast boosts, then slower. Best use: concept drafts and splash/marketing comps, then PixelLab or the pixel pass for anything that ships. SOUND, MUSIC, VOICE. Stable Audio Open 1.0 (open weights, runs locally, up to 47 s, better at sound effects than music; Stability Community License, check stability.ai/license for commercial use); ElevenLabs free 10,000 credits a month (about 50 sound effects or 10 minutes of voice) but no commercial licence on free (Starter $6/month has it: your call); Suno free 50 credits/day (about 10 songs) but non-commercial and few downloads, so reference tracks only. For the shipped music (D17) CC0 packs remain the safe route. VIDEO (trailer, A3). Kling via fal stays the plan; it needs a paid key and a cap (below). PAID KEYS (only if you choose): OpenAI (platform.openai.com, set a monthly budget and alerts at 50% / 80% first) and fal.ai (prepaid credits, load the smallest top-up or none until A2); name each key bramblewood-local, store as OPENAI_API_KEY / FAL_KEY in your environment, tell me 'keys are set' and I check only that they exist, then run one test through tools/art/pixelize.py. Recommended order: free tiers first (OpenRouter free + Google AI Studio + DeepL API Free + CodeRabbit), routed through LiteLLM or OpenRouter; paid OpenAI / fal keys only when A2 or A3 go ahead. items.title: Spend about $7-15 to train a Bramblewood pixel LoRA and test it on 10 cards?
items.body: What a Bramblewood pixel LoRA is: a small add-on trained on our own card art so a general image model (FLUX.2 [dev], trained on fal) draws new cards in the same house style; PixelLab stays the main source and heroes stay PixelLab. Data: 20-40 of the best existing PixelLab cards from art/cards (633 PNGs, 256x256 today), picked for one coherent look: same outline weight, same palette (tools/art/palette.json), a spread of subjects (mammal, bird, insect, structure), no text in the image, no watermarked stock. Each image gets a short caption in the style of docs/art-style-prompts.md with a trigger word (for example 'bwpixel') so the style can be called on and off. About half a day of curation, which I can do from the repo; you pick or veto the 30. Tool options: (a) fal's FLUX.2 trainer (hosted, no GPU, upload a zip of images and captions, about 1,000-2,000 steps, roughly $6.40 per 1,000 steps on fal's list, so about $6-13 per training run plus about a few cents per generated image; check the current price on fal's page before any run); (b) Replicate's FLUX trainer (similar, per-run pricing); (c) a local or rented GPU with ai-toolkit/kohya (cheaper per run, but needs a rented GPU and setup time; not worth it for a 10-card test). Recommendation: (a), because A1 already puts a fal key and cap in place. Cost range: a first test is about $7-15 in total (one 1,000-step training plus 10-40 generations), and a retrain with fixes is the same again; a full set of Maps 9-10 cards afterwards is cents per card. All of it stays under the cap you set in A1; nothing runs without your OK on the amount. Test plan on 10 cards: (1) train once on the 30; (2) generate the 10 test cards, chosen from existing cards whose PixelLab art we already like, so each result can be set beside the original (a mix: 3 small animals, 2 birds, 2 insects, 1 structure, 1 large beast, 1 fantasy creature); (3) run each through `tools/art/pixelize.py` (nearest-neighbour downscale to the 160 px grid, palette snap, outline clean-up); (4) review in the hub's Visual Library as 'proposed', scoring each on outline, palette, readable silhouette at card size and fit beside the PixelLab neighbours; (5) pass if at least 7 of 10 are usable with at most a pixel pass and one retry, fail otherwise; (6) if it passes, spend the same amount on the Maps 9-10 cards and the Home sprites that wait on PixelLab; if it fails, delete the LoRA and keep PixelLab only. Needs from you: A1 done, a yes on the training spend, and a veto pass over the 30 picks. | 2026-10-29 (owner 00:10: "Write the chance of this passing, let's say we have 100 artwork we like"): with 100 liked cards as training data (more than the 20-40 planned, so a stronger style signal; about 2,000-3,000 steps, so roughly $13-19 per run at fal's list price, check before any run): my estimate is about 65% that the 10-card test passes (7 or more of the 10 accepted after our usual palette quantise and nearest-neighbour downscale). Style match (palette, outline weight, framing) is the easy part: about 85%. The risk is a true pixel grid: FLUX draws "pixel-look" art with soft, uneven pixels, so each image needs the quantise/downscale clean-up, and roughly 1 in 2 single generations will be usable, so expect 2-3 tries per card. Subjects far from the training set (dinosaurs, golems) fail more often. A 10-card test tells us this for about one run's cost; Claude does not buy the credits.

items.title: Cards that cost 3+ Lumber don't pay off
items.body: Cards costing 3+ Lumber (all five dragons included) score ~38% in simulation. 2026-10-09, taking the default on 'continue': all 30 got an arrival effect (dragons breathe 4 on every enemy; brutes hit the enemy opposite for 2× their cost; Elder Willow, Elderhorn Monarch and Riverworks Bastion refund 2 Lumber; the slow small ones delay the enemy opposite by 2 Wait). It didn't move them: the real cause is that Lumber only comes from discarding cards, so a 4-cost card costs five cards in all. Tested a passive income with the CPU saving properly: +1 Lumber every 2 rounds gives cost-2 cards 75%, cost-3+ 51%, dragons 60% (free cards fall to ~24%, as cheap cards should); every round is too much (dragons 96%); every 3 rounds is too little (45%).
options: Keep discard-only Lumber; make big cards cheaper
items.outcome: You chose no free Lumber income (it inflates Lumber costs). Instead, cards that give Lumber or draws (Beaver Lumberjack: +2 Lumber; Courier Pigeon: draw 1), plus a day/night cycle and field cards to make rounds vary. items.title: The stat budget is v5: (Base + L/5)(1 + L/30), Level 0 Base - 1
items.body: Budget v4 ((Base - 1 + L)(1 + L/20), 09:52) made the Forge curve far too strong (the mean card +228% by Lv 10). Which formula replaces it, and does its linear Level term favour weak cards?
options: v5 with L/3, the owner's example (Base 14: 14.8 at Lv 1, 23.1 at Lv 10)
items.default: v5, L/3 unless it favours weak cards too much
items.outcome: Owner 13:52: "Oh shit to the balance. That's too much. ... maybe instead: (Base + L/3) * (1 + L/30) ... Level 0 gives an additional minus 1." 13:54: "if you think it favours weak cards too much (low rarity, wait, or resource count), then change it to L/4 or L/5." Measured (docs/balance/level-curve-2026-10-19c.md): weak cards' Lv 10 stat growth is 1.82x the strong cards' with L/3, 1.74x with L/4, 1.65x with L/5 (Rare+ with 3+ Wait and 3+ Lumber; 1.46 / 1.40 / 1.31 against Rare+ with 3+ Wait or Lumber). None meets the 1.3x rule, so the budget uses L/5, the closest (levelLinDiv in bramblewood-budget.js and canonical/skill-costs.json). Most of the gap comes from the absolute conversion, not the divisor. Budget v5: N = (Base + L/5) x (1 + L/30) for Level 1 and up, Base - 1 at Level 0; Base = 20 + Rarity + 6W + 0.5W^2 + 4 Lumber + 0.4 Lumber^2 + Ritual points. The Forge curve keeps majors 4/7/10, minor 2 and the limit break 11 on v5's gain: the mean card is +6% at Lv 2, +27% at Lv 4 and +96% at Lv 10.

items.title: Bloom's copy: it can't bloom, and it arrives like a played card
items.body: Your 11:23 and 17:34 #3. Built: Bloom - {conditions} is once per unit: the first round its conditions hold a copy of it grows beside it, and the copy gains +1/+1 (your 19:30: "bloom only gives the new one +1/+1, not itself"; the unit is unchanged). The copy has the unit's Attack and Health with every change made without counters, plus 1/+1, minus its damage; no counters or statuses. The copy is marked as a copy and never blooms itself (else one bloom would chain into a field of copies), arrives with its printed Wait, and leaves no card in the graveyard when it dies (so it can't feed Remember / Grave Call). Say if the copy should bloom too, arrive Ready, or go to the graveyard.
options: The copy can't bloom; printed Wait; no graveyard card (built)
The copy can bloom once too
items.default: The copy can't bloom; printed Wait; no graveyard card (built)

items.title: Bloom with no free slot beside it
items.body: Built: the copy grows only in a free slot right beside the unit (a coin flip when both sides are free; in a raid's middle / back row, beside it in that row). With both neighbours taken it doesn't bloom yet and tries again at the next round's start, so the bloom is never wasted. Alternatives: bloom anyway with no copy (nothing happens then), or put the copy in the nearest free slot of the row (the Spawn rule).
options: Wait and try again next round (built)
The nearest free slot in the row
items.default: Wait and try again next round (built)

items.title: Armor flattens after 3: re-price Armor 4 and 5?
items.body: SKILL2-3 asked to measure Armor 4-5 first. The pipeline measured them (node tools/pipeline/run.sh measure --skills armor=4,armor=5; 200 fights each, the interval already narrow; docs/balance/pipeline/measures.json): Armor 4 is worth 4.95 [4.64, 5.52] stat points and Armor 5 5.01 [4.75, 5.58], against 6.75 and 7.84 on the canon curve 2.65 x N^0.675. So the worth runs 2.65 / 4.23 / 4.84 / 4.95 / 5.01 for Armor 1-5: it saturates, the opposite of your 'slightly exponential, 5 armor nullifies most damage' (ENG9-9). No in-play card carries Armor 4 or 5, so no card is affected today; the table is unchanged (record only).
options: Keep the canon curve (Armor 4 and 5 stay at 6.75 and 7.84, dear next to what they measure)
Cap the curve: Armor 4 and 5 priced at their measure, about 5.0 (a table edit through the pipeline price step; no card changes)
Keep your rule's shape above 3 as a design price, ignoring the measure
items.default: Cap the curve: Armor 4 and 5 priced at their measure, about 5.0 (a table edit through the pipeline price step; no card changes)
items.outcome: Coordinator: keep the canon curve for now; no in-play card has Armor 4+. The Armor 4-5 measures (4.95 / 5.01) are on record; re-price when a card first uses Armor 4+.

items.title: Flying and Evasive: the measure reads x1.17 / x1.16, not x1.13
items.body: SKILL2-2 set Flying and Evasive to 'the measured x1.13', and SPEED1 wrote x1.13 into MISS_MULT_BY as decided. The pipeline's price step now derives the multiplier from the measure itself and disagrees: the multiplier m acts on the carriers' stat terms (mean 3A + H = 20.83 on the canon's six carriers), so m = 1 + worth / 20.83 = 1 + 3.56 / 20.83 = x1.17 [1.16, 1.18] for Flying and 1 + 3.42 / 20.83 = x1.16 [1.15, 1.18] for Evasive. The SKILL2 write-up got x1.13 by reading the 10.4-point price on the carriers as 0.39 x 26.7; tools/skill_costs.js had priced it at a flat x1.5 (0.5 x 20.83 = 10.4), so the 26.7 never existed. At x1.13 a flyer's stat terms are priced 0.04 x 20.8 = about 0.8 points (4%) under what the measure says. The 4 flyer lifts made by the refit (Mountain Goat Climber, Swordbill Challenger, Ash Cloud Condor, Plains Zebra) were made at x1.13.

rules.intro: The owner's directions (Oct 21) on rewards, sources, the road's eras and its bosses, recorded by package RP (docs/balance/rewards-pass-2026-10-21.md, docs/map-recommendations-2026-10-21.md). Pinned by `tests/rewards-pass-2026-10-21.js`.
items: **Skirmish rewards are never pack cards; faction rewards are their own category** ("Be strict on what is a Skirmish reward (these CANNOT be pack rewards) and which are faction rewards"): every card is exactly one of a skirmish reward (source map), a pack card, a faction reward (the Factions pool, tier 11, in no pack), or a raid / smith / nest / base / quest / secret / Easter egg / materia card, or awaitingSource.

**Most Otters and Hummingbirds are faction rewards, given with skirmish progress and some achievements**: a main map's last fight, every 8th first clear, Map 0's 0-2 faction pack, the 3-2 ambush and the listed achievements hand them out (FACTION_REWARD_TRACK).

**Faction rewards give the lowest rarity first, until a critical mass of faction cards received (duplicates count)**: Uncommon after 25, Rare after 15 more and not before Map 14, Very Rare after 10 more and much later (Map 25 proposed); the later steps (Super Rare 60 / Map 30, Epic 70 / 35, Heroic 80 / 40, Unique+ 90 / 50) are proposals. The thresholds are constants (FACTION_RARITY_GATES).
**Only plain cards (no skills) as rewards at the start** (Maps 0-1), with **Lumber introduced on Map 1** by one Lumber card (the Badger Lumberjack on 1-4).
**Devilry is found on Map 66, Ecclesia on Map 77, Evomax from Map 30**: no card of those lines is obtainable before (they wait as awaitingSource).
**The eras: 20-40 is stronger, more advanced versions of the 0-20 animals, and maybe some extinct animals that resemble today's; 40+ has legit dinosaurs; 50+ is magic.**

**Submaps: one unique card each, the rest built from cards the player already has, and unlocked quite late** (Smugglers' Grotto after Map 7; every side map off Maps 0-19 opens at least four maps after its parent, its fights counting as that map).
**Skill introduction is gentle and strict: two new skills a map at most; Maps 21-40 are about using the skills already learnt** (new skills again past Map 40).
**5 world bosses and 1 super world boss for Maps 0-100.**
**Bosses from Map 5 onwards, so at least 95 bosses and 100+ elites, not counting the submaps.**
**Limit break always balances a card to the next series's standard.**
**Map x 0.2 in N gives importance to new cards balanced in the late game** (the stat budget's map term; package BF5 builds it, with vanilla cards x1.05).

rules.intro: The owner's notes (23:05) on a far-future map and the Legendary ability tier. Pinned by `tests/legendary-2026-10-19.js`.
items: **Shadow of the Valley of Death is a very far future map.** It is not on the road yet and nothing is planned for it now. The Pall Wraith (`pall-wraith`, Cast Darkness + Darksight) lives in the Eye of the Volcano (20-A, the 20-A-2 Wraith Vents deck and card reward) until that map exists.

**Legendary abilities are a tier of their own.** A skill or passive marked `legendary: true` (PASSIVE_DEFS / SKILL_DEFS in `arena_app.js`, and `canonical/skill-costs.json`) shows a gold Legendary tag on the card's line, in the Skills Codex and in the card's glossary: "A legendary power. Rarely found on cards you can own — dragons are the exception." They are typically not given to cards players can get, except dragons. Legendary now: True Strike ("White Dragon's True Strike is legendary in itself"), Supreme and Supreme Tide.

**True Strike is affected by Legendary dodges.** It still ignores every plain miss or dodge: Darkness, Blind, Sun-shy, Night-blind, Evasive, Swift, Flying, Prey, Tide-evade, canopy, Smoke, Fog, Sandstorm, Ashy, Slippery, Shadow and Illusory. A Legendary dodge still rolls against it as against anyone. It still can't hit Invisible.

**Illusory is not Legendary** ("the illusory dodge is a token thing anyway, so it's not particularly legendary"). No dodge is Legendary yet. The engine hook is ready: a dodge source is Legendary when its reason is in `LEGENDARY_DODGES` or the defender's effect value carries `legendary: true` (e.g. `evasive: {legendary: true}`, `illusory: {chance: 0.5, legendary: true}`) (`legendaryDodge` in `bramblewood-engine.js`).

rules.intro: The owner's answers (20:31) to the design review's questions on triggers, now rules of the engine (`bramblewood-engine.js`). Pinned by `tests/trigger-layers-2026-10-19.js`.
items: **Trigger chains stop at 5 layers (layers, not count).** The original event's triggers are layer 1. A trigger that goes off while another trigger is resolving is one layer deeper. Layers 1 to 5 resolve; a 6th-layer trigger does not fire (`TRIGGER_LAYER_CAP = 5`). Any number of triggers at the same layer (siblings) all resolve.

**A death sweep counts in layers too.** The deaths settled in a sweep's first pass fire layer-1 triggers (counted from where the sweep starts: a sweep opened inside a layer-2 trigger starts at layer 3). The deaths those triggers cause settle in the next pass, one layer deeper. The sweep's 6-pass limit is the cap plus one: the 6th pass clears the bodies and fires no triggers.

**A unit killed during a death sweep dies in the next pass** (Claude's fix, 2026-10-19). A unit killed by a death effect (Nova, Landslide, an On Death or On Ally Die trigger) dies properly, with its own death effects, graveyard and Darkness. It used to vanish with no death at all.
**Tokens fire death triggers.** A token's own On Death fires, and its allies fire On Ally Die for it, like any unit.
**Evasive covers both.** It dodges half of single-target attacks and skills.
**Simultaneous triggers resolve in board order:** the first player's units, then the second player's, lane by lane (left, centre, right).
**Units dying in the same sweep don't see each other's On Ally Die.** Units that die in the same pass of a sweep are all gone together: only units still alive in that pass fire it.

**Summoned and token units fire On Ally Spawn, not On Ally Played.** A unit an effect puts on the board (a token, a summon, a split, a hatch) is spawned. On Ally Played is for a card played from hand (leaders included).
**A unit's own death is not an ally death.** It fires its own On Death, never its own On Ally Die.
**0 healing fires no heal trigger.** Healing a unit already at full Health fires no On Heal, On Healed or On Ally Healed.

rules.intro: The owner's rules (23:32) on Freeze and Confuse, now rules of the engine (`bramblewood-engine.js`, package FZ). Pinned by `tests/fz-2026-10-19.js`.
items: **A unit frozen before its turn arrives fails to take its action.** Frozen earlier in the round (an earlier unit's Freeze or Ice Arrow), it skips its place in that round's order: no swing, no shot, no On Attack, no on-hit skill. That freeze is then spent: it melts at this round's end, so Freeze N costs N actions (Claude's reading, 2026-10-19: it used to swing anyway and then lose the next round).
**Frozen after it acted** (a later hit that round, from the opponent's units) **it skips its next round**, then thaws, as before. Frozen before the round starts, it skips that round.

**Confused: 1 in 2 that each of its triggers, skills and actions fails to activate.** Every trigger, every on-hit chance skill, and every action (its swing, its shots, a reserve strike, a Counterattack, a Sentry or Ambush strike) rolls on its own; on a fail nothing happens and the log says "😵 X is confused and fumbles." The rolls use the match's seeded random, so sims and replays repeat.

**Confuse's swing (Claude's choice, 2026-10-19):** Confuse had no other effect on the attack, so the attack counts as an action: a fumbled swing is no swing at all (no On Attack, no on-hit skills, no Bleed tick). A swing that goes off still rolls each of its on-hit chance skills, as before.

rules.intro: The owner's notes (21:26) on emoji with cultural meaning.
items: **Ward uses 🧿 Nazar.** When a Ward skill is made (e.g. Prayer Ward in docs/gameplay-ideas-2026-10-19.md, or a ward against Blind / curses), its icon is the nazar, or a white/yellow East Asian paper talisman (no emoji exists, so that would be a drawn icon).

**🪬 Hamsa is never a generic effect icon.** It carries real cultural and religious meaning, so it appears only inside one animal society's own identity (its cards, banner or rites), never as an effect any unit can get. Which society is still open.

rules.intro: The owner's note (00:07): "Healing & the like: if there's nothing to heal, it doesn't occur, and no animation plays." Now a rule of the engine (`bramblewood-engine.js`) and the board (`arena_app.js`). Pinned by `tests/hn-2026-10-19.js`.
items: **A heal with nothing to heal doesn't happen.** Every heal-like effect (the Heal action, Regeneration, Bloom, Nursing, Healing N, Leech, Carrion, Banana, Cower (Flee), Spring Rain, the Herb Refinery, Herbalist's bonus, Rebuild and the Rebuild bramble action, the bramble's own regeneration, Cure) on a unit already at full Health (a bramble at full Health) heals nothing and shows nothing: no heal event, no battle-log line, no floating "+0", no heal look or sound, and no beat in the replay. (A Cower (Flee) unit still backs off, only without a heal number; a Mend spell is still cast, without the green heal look when no one is hurt.)
**0 healing fires no heal trigger** (kept from the trigger rules above): no On Heal, On Healed or On Ally Healed.

**A Heal or Rebuild trigger with nothing to heal doesn't go off.** Its trigger rune isn't shown, and a "once" Heal trigger isn't used up (it waits for a real wound). One that paid a cost first (Burn 1 Lumber) did go off.

**Bleed counts as something to heal** (Claude's choice, the recommended one). A heal on a full-Health unit that Bleeds happens: it stanches the Bleed (the Bleed-removal look only, 🩹 -N 🩸), with no green heal look, no "+0" and no heal triggers. Regeneration is the exception and keeps the owner's 2026-10-14 rule ("Do not regenerate when the unit is at full health"): at full Health it doesn't stanch either.

**Old fights and replays too.** The board skips any 0-amount heal event that still turns up (a saved fight or replay from before this rule): no look, no sound, no beat, no log line (`emptyHealEvent` in `arena_app.js`).

rules.intro: The owner's rules (00:19): "Revive is true death, but Rescue no." and "Quiet Contemplation on Map 21's boss: no 2x and re-enablement effects." Now rules of the engine (`bramblewood-engine.js`, package RV), replacing the earlier rule that a Revive death was no death (no death triggers, only the killer's On Kill). Pinned by `tests/rv-2026-10-19.js`.
items: **Revive is a true death.** The first death, the one Revive answers, happens in full: the unit's On Death, its allies' On Ally Die (and Berserk, Divine Retribution, Hive Mind), the killer's On Kill and kill stat (Crown of Thorns, Midas Touch), Bounty, Darkness from the loss, the Ritual count, the deaths stat, Amore, Carrion, On Death: Spawn, Landslide, Nova, and the trip to the graveyard (or the Removal Zone). Then the unit returns: out of that zone, into its own slot, at 1 Health with every status cleared. Its second death is final (the Removal Zone), as before.

**What would replace the body doesn't happen on a Revive death** (Claude's call): no Relic 1/1 (the unit itself comes back; its final death leaves the Relic), no Crystallise crystal, no Meiosis split. An On Death: Spawn token goes beside it, not into its slot. Its equipment stays on; its Prayer tokens are gone with the death.

**Revive loops stop at the layer cap.** Revive is once per unit. The triggers a Revive death sets off are ordinary trigger layers of the death sweep, so a revive whose death kills another reviving unit, and so on, stops at layer 5 (`TRIGGER_LAYER_CAP`) like any chain. A Nullify kill still gets no Revive.

**Rescue is not a death.** A unit moved or saved before it would die fires none of the above: no death event, no On Death, On Ally Die, On Kill, Bounty, Darkness, Ritual count or deaths stat, and its Revive stays unspent. Today that is Shield Call (the ally steps aside and a shield takes the skill) and Guardian (an adjacent protector takes the hit); no effect called Rescue exists yet.

**Quiet Contemplation (the Cathedral Eagle's fight, 21-6): nothing happens twice.** Doubling, off: Headwind (a Flyer's triggers and skills twice), Twin Strike and Frenzy's second swing, Twin Shot's second arrow, Twin (the copy on arrival), Echoing Wood's copy, Crit, an Expose counter's crit (the counter is still used up), Rage's ×2, Mighty's ×2, Tall Grass's double Backstab / Pounce, Supreme Tide (plain Tide bonuses instead) and Double Time (1 play a turn, no second-player bonus for it). Re-enablement, off: every extra turn (Fast Forward N, the Tailwind spell's turn, a strong wind's Tailwind, a Swimmer's Quick Attack on a Flood) and Wildpath's Second Pitch. Both sides.

**Quiet Contemplation leaves these alone** (Claude's reading; say if any should go): plain Wait cuts (Hasten, Reduce Wait), multi-target skills (Volley, Sweep, Fork, a trigger's N targets), the target's own weakness or Fragile (double damage taken), Boomerang's return (it is that round's attack), Banana / Durian snacks, a Charge's cycle, Rage's half damage taken, and Revive (once, and a true death).

rules.intro: Package GI (owner 00:19: "continue with action items, and considering our gameplay-ideas ... After running through the ideas, create what you want to create"): the skills and field effects built from docs/gameplay-ideas-2026-10-19.md, now rules of the engine (`bramblewood-engine.js`, the Package GI block). Only POOL example cards carry them; no live card or map does yet. Details: docs/gameplay-ideas-built-2026-10-19.md. Pinned by `tests/gi-2026-10-19.js`.
items: **A trigger can target the card it is about** (the owner's question 7 in gameplay-ideas-2026-10-19: yes, it targets the played card). A trigger's subject is the ally played (or the unit that died, was healed, got Ready or moved): `sub:'subject'` is that unit, `sub:'subjectFacing'` the unit facing it, and `filterKin` keeps only a subject that is the acting unit's Kin.

**Kin Rally N** (On Ally Played (Kin): that ally +N/+N) and **Pack Howl N** (On Ally Played (Wolf): Bleed N on the enemy facing it) are ordinary On Ally Played triggers: off while the unit is Waiting, Stunned, Frozen or Asleep; Confused fumbles them; the 5-layer cap holds; a card played from hand only (a token is On Ally Spawn). A Changeling passes both filters. Nobody facing the Wolf: no Bleed.

**Hunter N is one keyword with a status picker**: Poisoned (the default), Bleeding, Wet or Exposed; Shatter stays the Frozen case. Exposed is read before the hit uses up its counter. Hunter and **Executioner N** (strictly below half Health) add to hits and shots, never to a status tick or a bramble.

**Detonate** (Claude's reading): its hit or shot deals the target's whole Poison as extra damage, 1 for 1, then that Poison is gone. Poison ticks at the round's start first, so it cashes in what the tick left.

**Proliferate N**: from round 2, at each round's start, up to N Poisoned enemies (picked at random) each give 1 Poison to a random unit beside them. It spreads (the carrier keeps its own); poison-proof units never catch it. A passive, so it works while its unit is Waiting.
**Brittle** (a status from Brittle N hits) counts as Frozen for Shatter only: the unit still acts and its Wait still ticks. It wears off like Webbed; Revive clears it, Cure doesn't (as Webbed).
**Prayer Ward N**: Armor N while the unit holds Prayer tokens (the player's own offering tokens are not on the unit, so they don't count). Its icon is 🧿 Nazar (owner, 2026-10-18 21:26).

**Field Breaker N** (Claude's scope): when it arrives, the field's round-start effects are skipped for the next N rounds, for both sides: every Field effects 2 and 3 tick (the hazards, the Leylines' gifts and burn, Haunted, Mirage, Wave, Consternation, and the three new fields), Swamp Fever, the Tide-spout and the volcano's eruptions, comets and lava. Day and night, the Tide, Darkness, wind, the always-on field rules (Sandstorm misses, Ashy, Slippery ...) and a played field card go on. Two breaks don't add up: the later end wins.

**Spore Cloud** (for The Morel Hollow): from round 2, one random unit a side that isn't poison-proof falls Asleep for the round, as Sleep 1, so the Sleep cap (N+1) holds it at 2 at most; a hit wakes it.
**Thunderstorm N** (2; for Coral Current): from round 2, lightning (shock) strikes one random unit a side for N; each Wet counter adds 1, shock Resist halves it.
**Tangled Roots** (for the Kelp Mangroves): from round 2, one random unit a side that isn't Flying or a Structure is Webbed for the round.
**Crab Trap is data, not a rule** (Claude's call): a Crab Claws card with Hunter 1 (Wet) (the pool card Tidepool Trapper Crab). Crab Claws itself is unchanged, so no live crab changed.

**Skipped, each against a standing rule or the owner's earlier no**: Isolation (fights Lone Wolf), Rescue Chain and Death Spiral (loops), a generic Contagion (folded into Proliferate), and Hallowed Ground and Blood in the Water (left for the placement phase: small-engine but each one fight).

rules.intro: Package SK1 (owner 21:36, new combat skills; 21:56: "if you can and it makes sense, feel free to use triggers and actions. if they dont suffice, add the required trigger or action."): the design notes the owner gave with the skills, and the rules SK1 built. Rules in `bramblewood-engine.js` (the Package SK1 block); pinned by `tests/skills-sk1-2026-10-19.js`.
items: **Maps 21–40 are mostly about using the skills already learnt** (owner 21:36): new skills arrive past Map 40 (Punish is the first one held for then); Maps 21–40 lean on the skills a player has met by Map 20.

**After each map has an appropriate set of canonical animals, arrange skills and stats, relying on what's already there and changing only if required** (owner 21:36): skills and stats follow the map's animals, reusing the existing ones first.

**Skills are triggers × actions where they fit** (owner 21:56): Sentry N = On Enemy Enters (Facing): Damage N; Expose N / Exploit N / Venom Pulse N = On Hit: Expose / Exploit / Poison Tick N; Spoils N = On Kill (Creature): Buff itself +0/+N. New triggers On Enemy Enters (Facing), On Hit, On Kill (Creature); new actions Exploit and Poison Tick.

**Expose is about hiding, Exploit about damage** (owner 21:36): Expose N strips the target's hiding for N rounds (Invisible, Evasive, Smoke, Shadow, Stealth; Flying and Swift still dodge); Exploit N puts N tokens on, each later hit +1 and one token used (the old Expose crit counters' role).

**Cure / Heal / Cleanse** (owner 21:36): Cure removes Poison only; Heal restores Health only (no Bleed stanch); Cleanse (and Renewal, its shorthand) removes the physical debuffs: Bleed, Scar, Corrosion, Brittle, Exposed, Exploit, Shocked (Vulnerable), Staggered and Daunt (Weakness), a Perforate's shredded Armor (Rend), and a future Burn. Not Freeze, Stun, Sleep, Paralyze, Blind, Tipsy, Confused, Decay or Poison (Claude's call on Burn and Freeze). A cell curse still comes off first. Phoenix Fledgling keeps its intent with Renewal + Cure 2.

**Siege N = the old Demolisher and the old Siege** (owner 21:36): +N on Structures and on swings at the bramble; `demolisher` stays an alias for old saves and overrides (the higher of the two when both).

**Isolation is a drawback** (owner 21:36: "(4, 3, 2, 1, or 0) - range = 2"): allies within 2 columns, 0/1/2/3/4+ give −4/−3/−2/−1/0 Attack and Health (flat, Claude's call over −50%), a table parameter; its S is negative, like the payments.

**Punish N is held behind a flag** (owner: an advanced skill for Map 40+, design open): the recommended design (docs/skills-punish-proposal.md) is built behind `rules.punishSkill` / engine `flags.punish` and is on no card.
**Every SK1 number is a parameter** (owner: the numbers may be halved): the engine's SK1_DEF defaults, a card's own N, and `makeSimEngine(..., {sk1:{...}})` to change the defaults in one place.

rules.intro: Package SK2b (owner 23:43: "I want to make resources really a strategic move. Not a simple - just put."): the three-tier economy and the cost principle. Details: docs/economy-resources-2026-10-19.md. Pinned by `tests/skills-sk2b-2026-10-19.js`.
items: **Strong creatures can be low costed - and their power is that they are low costed** (the owner, 23:43). A cheap strong card is a design tool, not a balance error: its strength is tempo. Costly cards are strong because they need an economy, and the economy is what the opponent can attack. The budget is not bent for such cards; they are a deliberate, marked class (recommendation, not applied).

**Three tiers, each paid with the one below** (all On Turn Start × Gain, while Ready): Milling N gives N Lumber free; Quarry N pays 1 Lumber for N Stone; Smelter N pays 2 Lumber + 2 Stone for 1 Metal, up to N times. The ratios are parameters (SK2_DEFAULTS). The Petrified Tree stays the expensive no-input Stone source.

**A trigger can have a price** (t.pay, Lumber / Stone / Metal / Uranium): it goes off only if its player holds all of it, and pays after every other gate, so a fizzle costs nothing. A conversion is paid whole or not at all; can't pay, nothing happens. Units pay in the upkeep's order, so a Quarry acting first can feed a Smelter the same turn.
**Smelter, not Forge-works** (Claude's call): the Forge is already the card-upgrade screen.
